adjustments.justification: Largest single deviation from a liquid market in the set. Polymarket's $107M 'Next French Presidential Election' book prices Bardella at 25.5% to win outright and 72% to reach the runoff; adding Le Pen and any other RN-endorsed candidate gets the RN family to roughly 30-33%, not 45%. The model runs ~1.4x the market on a heavily traded, well-specified question with no informational edge — the 'first round is near-certain' argument is already fully priced (72%), so the disagreement is entirely about the runoff, where the market implies ~35% conditional and the model implies ~62%. Its base-rate anchor (0 wins in 3 runoffs; linear +12pt/cycle reaching ~53%) is naive linear extrapolation of a bounded, saturating series. Factual update on the item the model flagged as unverified: the Paris Court of Appeal ruled 7 July 2026 — conviction upheld, ineligibility cut to 45 months with 30 suspended, the 15 firm months already elapsed, so Le Pen IS eligible, with a Cour de Cassation ruling possible as late as April 2027. Net NEGATIVE for RN: it reopens an intra-RN candidate fight, Le Pen polls materially worse than Bardella, and a Cassation ruling weeks before the vote is a live tail risk. The model's own contrarian case calls this 'the most over-narrativized number in this set' and then declines to act on it.

Mechanical consequence of the 2027 revision — there is no French presidential election between 2027 and 2032, so p_2031 must equal p_2027. The equality is correctly specified; only the level is wrong.

62 given 45 implied a 31% conditional win in 2032. Keeping roughly that conditional (26%) on a 33% base gives ~50%. The conditional should arguably be lower than the 2027 number, not comparable: a fourth consecutive runoff loss in 2027 would damage Bardella specifically (37 and twice-beaten) and would be strong evidence the republican front still binds, so 2032 is not an independent redraw of the 2027 lottery.

COHERENCE, not level. The criterion is fully determined on 3 January 2027 ('when the new Congress convenes on 3 January 2027'). It cannot accrue probability from the 2028 or 2030 cycles — those are different Congresses. The stated reasoning ('small additional chances at 2028/2030 if 2026 somehow fails') directly contradicts the written criterion. All three horizons must carry the same number. I set the common value to 90 rather than 88 because the criterion is 'House AND/OR Senate': Polymarket's 86% is House-only, the Senate adds a small disjunctive increment even under high correlation, and Polymarket carries both a favourite-longshot bias and a documented 2024-vintage Republican lean on US races.
Same coherence fix — a question resolving on a fixed date in January 2027 must have a flat cumulative curve thereafter.

Mild UNDER-forecast via scope insensitivity in the generous direction: the analyst priced the House-only market (86%) then added only 2 points for a criterion that is explicitly disjunctive over two chambers. Even with heavy inter-chamber correlation, P(House or Senate) with House at 86-88% and Senate at 20-25% lands at 89-91%.

BASE RATE VIOLATION plus revealed-preference evidence the model collects and discards. The cited 7%/yr is an artefact of pooling 1957-2025: four of five invocations sit in the 1957-1968 civil-rights enforcement regime, structurally the opposite case (federal power used against state defiance of federal civil-rights orders). Post-1992 the count is zero in 34 years, including Katrina 2005 when Bush explicitly considered and declined. More decisively, we have ~13 months at what should be peak hazard: LA (Jun 2025), Chicago/Portland (autumn 2025), Minneapolis after a fatal ICE shooting plus a 2,400-agent surge (Jan 2026) — four maximal-provocation nodes, four explicit threats, zero invocations. 30% over 17 months requires ~22%/yr, roughly 3x the rate implied by 13 months of non-firing. The one genuinely new upward factor (the 23 Dec 6-3 ruling closing the 12406 route) is offset by that same ruling signalling how this Court would treat an IA proclamation, and by the near-certain loss of the House in November raising the price.

Preserves the model's correct declining-hazard shape — most mass belongs before January 2029 — while rebasing the level. 20 -> 30 implies ~2.9%/yr over 2028-2031, still a large multiple of the 0-in-34-years post-1992 record.
Rebased; the 2032-2036 increment (~1.5%/yr) is close to the long-run pooled base rate and is the one part of this curve that was already sensible.

Worst scope-insensitivity error in the set, and a conjunctive-coherence violation. The criterion requires FOUR things jointly: a governor issues an affirmative ORDER to block or detain federal personnel; an armed confrontation follows; it produces a death OR a gunpoint detention of an officer by the other side; and protest scuffles and litigation are explicitly excluded. Zero instances in ~150 years — including 1957 Little Rock and 1962 Ole Miss, where governors did deploy state forces to obstruct and it still ended without an exchange of fire. It is near-conjunctive on the Insurrection Act item: 7 against 30 implies a 23% conditional that a federal deployment escalates to a fatal or gunpoint state-federal standoff. Every historical analogue escalated the other way — states fold or litigate once federal force arrives. Conditional escalation should be 10-15% at most; against my revised IA number (20%), 3% is the coherent value. The model's own contrarian case makes exactly this argument and does not price it.

Scaled to preserve a ~15-20% conditional-escalation ratio against the revised Insurrection Act path. Blue-state governors' entire winning strategy is being the visibly lawful party, and they were rewarded for it 6-3 in December — the incentive gradient points hard away from this outcome. Governors also control Guard units simultaneously subject to federal call-up, so ordering them into confrontation risks fracturing their own chain of command.
Rebased consistently; the marginal 2032-2036 hazard the model implied (~0.6%/yr) was already near base rate, so the error is almost entirely in the front end.

BASE RATE: the model correctly finds zero clean instances in 235 years (<0.5%/yr) and then applies a ~17x multiplier over a 17-month window. Too large given the observed record: four flagship losses at this Court in a single term, four grudging compliances, each via narrower relitigation — which the criterion explicitly excludes ('slow-walking with a colorable legal argument does not count'). The criterion further requires 30+ days of knowing non-compliance AND either judicial characterization as evasion or 3-of-5 wire/paper confirmation. The last 18 months are a run of NOs at maximum stress. 7% is still a ~10x multiplier on the historical rate.
Rebased at the same hazard shape (~1.9%/yr post-January 2029, itself a ~4x base-rate multiple to account for internalized norm erosion).
Rebased. The model's own line — 'note how often this has been predicted and not happened since 2017' — is the correct outside view and should have moved the number, not just the commentary.

Two compounding errors. (1) Arithmetic: the stated assumption is ~25%/yr, which over ~1.4 years to end-2027 gives 33%, not 42 — while the model's own 2036 figure (87%) back-solves to ~18%/yr. The three horizons are mutually inconsistent and inconsistent with the stated rate. (2) Base-rate inflation: of the four cited onsets, Sudan (~48m) and Ukraine (44m) both fall BELOW the 50m population threshold the criterion itself sets, and Ukraine 2014 was internationalized. The clean count is 2 (Ethiopia 2020, Myanmar 2021) in 16 years across ~28 eligible states = ~0.45%/country-year = ~12%/yr of at least one, not 18%. Applying the model's own 1.4x elevated-environment multiplier to the corrected base gives ~17-18%/yr, or ~24-26% over 1.4 years. UCDP's 1,000-battle-death threshold is also stricter than the vibe: it excludes criminal violence, which is why Mexico has never been coded despite exceeding that death toll for a decade.

~18%/yr decaying to ~16%/yr over 5.4 years, preserving the model's mean-reverting shape on the corrected base. The model also risks double-counting: Iran, Pakistan, Ethiopia, Nigeria and Egypt are named as candidates, but their individual onset probabilities are each modest and highly correlated with the same global-conflict factor, so the union is smaller than naive independence gives.

~15%/yr in the outer window. This horizon was the least wrong of the three because its implied hazard (18%/yr) already sat close to the corrected near-term rate — the error is concentrated in the front end.

SCOPE INSENSITIVITY: resolution requires the Mexican federal government to PUBLICLY STATE it did not consent. Sheinbaum's demonstrated strategy is the 'sovereign decision' framing that lets Washington act while Mexico avoids declaring a sovereignty violation — precisely the posture that makes this resolve NO even if strikes occur. The most likely real-world path (a drone strike on a cartel target with tacit or ambiguous Mexican acquiescence, followed by a carefully worded Mexican statement) fails the criterion. Layered on a base rate of zero in 110 years, 33% over 17 months (~25%/yr) is too high. 24% still encodes a very large inside-view adjustment for the Venezuela precedent and Trump's explicit 'start hitting land' statement.
Rebased; the model's declining-hazard shape after January 2029 is correct and preserved.
Rebased at the same outer-window hazard (~1%/yr).

UNDER-forecast via a flat-hazard error. The model uses a constant 3.5-4%/yr for a decade. Male mortality hazard rises roughly exponentially with age: ~2.5%/yr at 74 but ~5-6%/yr at 84. Cumulative 10-year mortality for a 74-year-old male with elite care is ~35-40% on its own; adding the model's own 1-2%/yr irregular-exit term gives 45-50%, not 39%. This is the classic mistake of annualizing a near-term hazard across a long horizon. The 2027 (5) and 2031 (19) figures are correct — the error appears only where the age curve bites, which is the diagnostic signature.

Same flat-hazard error, smaller magnitude. Xi turned 73 in June 2026; 10-year cumulative mortality with rising age-specific hazard is ~28-32%, plus ~0.5-1%/yr irregular removal, plus a path the model ignores entirely: the criterion is 'no longer General Secretary for any reason', which includes a MANAGED handover in which Xi designates a successor at the 21st Congress (Oct 2027) or the 22nd (2032) while retaining the CMC chairmanship — the Deng and Jiang templates. That is a real 'yes' path with no instability at all.

HAZARD SHAPE — the model front-loads badly. By end-2027 there is exactly ONE report in the window (DR2027, published ~March 2027, coding calendar-2026). V-Dem's Regimes-of-the-World threshold requires that national elections cease to be free and fair, and the single most probable candidate (the US) will by then have run a normal midterm that the incumbent party lost — the strongest possible coding evidence AGAINST a downgrade, as the model itself notes and then does not price. 22% for one report cycle against a ~5%/yr union-wide base rate is a 4x+ multiplier applied to the wrong year.

Slight UNDER-forecast once front-loading is removed. Five report cycles, ~30 eligible countries, with the US, Slovakia, Italy, Croatia and Slovenia all newly coded as autocratizing and Slovakia under Fico the cleanest Hungary-2018 analogue. The base rate is understated too: the model counts only Hungary and Turkey, omitting that V-Dem coded Poland as an electoral autocracy during the PiS period — 3 cases in ~35 years, not 2.

Clear UNDER-forecast. Eleven report cycles across ~30 countries. The corrected base rate (~5-7%/yr union-wide at NORMAL conditions) alone compounds to 43-55% over 11 years, and the model simultaneously asserts conditions are far above normal and a reinforcing backsliding-legitimacy spiral with strength 0.7. Stopping at 52% after eleven years of an acknowledged record-breaking autocratization wave means the implied hazard in years 6-11 falls below the unconditional historical rate — internally inconsistent with its own state_of_play.

Calendar check: the only genuine forcing node before end-2027 is the September 2026 Saxony-Anhalt and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern round. The 2027 Land calendar (Schleswig-Holstein, Lower Saxony, Bremen) is all western and structurally hostile to AfD, and there is no federal election until 2029. So 16% must be almost entirely the probability that the CDU breaks the firewall within months of the September vote — against the Thuringia/Saxony 2024 precedent (maximally awkward coalitions built specifically to avoid it) and Merz having staked his leadership on it. 11% is the right price for a single node.

UNDER-forecast against the model's own reference class. It cites 6 of 8 Western European radical-right parties crossing into government within 15 years of first passing 20% — that is 75% — and discounts to 65% for German exceptionalism. But the 2036 horizon contains three further full Land cycles INCLUDING the 2029 eastern round (Saxony, Thuringia, Brandenburg, where AfD already polls first) plus the 2029 and 2033 federal elections. The criterion is broad: ANY single Land ministerial post, or a written toleration agreement, at ANY level. One eastern CDU state party defecting resolves it. The ban-proceeding tail cuts the other way but is itself unlikely to succeed and would take years.

The model's own reasoning says the risk window is 2027-2029 'not now' (wartime conditions favour consensus arrangements) and then places 14% — over half its 2031 mass — inside the near window anyway. The criterion is demanding: a government controlling Tehran not deriving authority from velayat-e faqih, sustained 90 days. A provisional Leadership Council under Article 111 still derives from velayat-e faqih and resolves NO. The 'vacant >12 months' clause is the one genuinely broadening path, but the constitution mandates immediate Assembly action and the IRGC's institutional interest is in filling the office fast. Base-rate discipline: forecasts of Iranian regime termination have gone 0-for-8 across 1980-88, 1999, 2009, 2017-18, 2019, 2022-23 and 2025-26.

Modest trim, holding the model's correct shift of mass into the 2027-2029 window. This sits inside the range its own reference class supports (3-4 collapses in ~20 comparable ideological-regime transitions = 15-20% per transition over a decade).

37% sits above the top of the model's own cited reference-class range, once you account for the fact that the modal post-decapitation outcome it describes — a more militarized, less clerical, entirely intact Islamic Republic — resolves NO.

Internal inconsistency plus wave-decay. The stated forward rate is ~35%/yr, which compounds to 92% by 2031 and 98.7% by 2036 — not the stated 80 and 89. The three numbers actually encode a hazard falling from ~35% to ~22% to ~18%/yr, contradicting the single stated rate. On the merits the declining path is right and the level too high: 2024 and 2025 produced 1 and 2 successful coups, the long-run rate is ~25%, and the supply-exhaustion argument is strong — Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger, Guinea and Guinea-Bissau are already juntas, and junta-on-junta palace reshuffles frequently fall outside Powell-Thyne successful-coup coding. ~28%/yr near-term is defensible.

~28%/yr decaying toward ~22%/yr over 5.4 years. Note also that the threshold is a CALENDAR-year count of 3+, which is lumpier than a rate: a year with 2 coups in December and 1 the following January resolves NO twice.
~20%/yr in the outer window, close to the long-run historical rate the model itself identifies (~25% of years hit 3+). Small trim only — this item was among the better-calibrated in the set.

The model correctly notes the recent five-year rate is ~15%/yr versus the 26%/yr 1995-2025 pooled rate (inflated by 9/11 and the 2015-16 jihadist cluster), then prices the near window at ~21%/yr anyway. The clean domestic-ideological >=10-fatality count for 2020-2025 is one (Buffalo 2022) in six years. Event counts are rising in the low-lethality categories — vandalism, arson, threats — while the lethality series is flat, and the model's own note on the corresponding continuous variable says explicitly 'do not treat this as a proxy for deaths'. 22% (~16%/yr) matches the recent rate with a modest upward tilt for the mobilization environment. The 2031 and 2036 figures already imply a sensibly declining 16% and 13%/yr and should be left alone.

The model states outright that 11% 'may be too high' and then keeps it. Hungary — the only member whose government ever flirted with exit — just installed an emphatically pro-EU supermajority; Slovak public opinion is strongly pro-membership; RN abandoned Frexit in 2017 and Bardella has not revived it; net fiscal recipients have overwhelming material reasons to stay. The 1-per-1,000-member-years base rate is itself inflated by a single case (UK) uniquely enabled by an opt-out-heavy, non-euro, non-Schengen island membership no current member replicates. The real risk — permanent unanimity vetoes and Article 7 stalemate — is explicitly outside this criterion.

Severity is mis-scaled relative to the realistic instance. The only plausible candidates are small-to-mid net recipients (Slovakia ~5.4m, ~1% of EU GDP). The model's own note says hollowing-out from within 'would do more damage than a small member leaving' — which is inconsistent with scoring that small member's exit at 8, level with a fatal US federal-state armed clash and Iranian regime collapse.

Minor. The criterion's cheapest trigger (an FEC filing) is procedurally trivial and its window is mostly 2027, as are state ballot-access deadlines — so 5% by end-2027 versus 10% ever leaves half the mass in the narrow Jan-Aug 2028 window, which is backwards. Given Trump's own 'probably not', his ruling out the VP workaround, his statement that Vance would be favoured, Vance at 35-46% in primary polling with markets near 44%, age 82 in 2028, and a post-1951 base rate of exactly zero, 4% is right for the near window.
Small trim for the same reasons; the flat 2031-to-2036 profile is correctly specified since the event can only occur in the 2028 cycle.

Mild UNDER-forecast in the outer window. 28 by 2031 and 35 by 2036 implies only a 10% conditional chance across the whole post-2029 cycle (an election due ~2033-34) given Reform fails in 2029. Too harsh: unless Reform collapses entirely, a party polling 24-29% that contests a general election as a major force retains materially better than a 10% shot at the following one. The 2027 (3) and 2031 (28) figures are defensible and I am leaving them — the criterion is narrower than the vibe suggests (it requires a Reform MP actually appointed PM, so 'largest party but cannot form a government' resolves NO), which offsets the poll-lead optimism.

coherence_violations: politics_dem_control_a_chamber_2027 — HARD VIOLATION. The resolution criterion is fully determined on 3 January 2027 ('when the new Congress convenes on 3 January 2027'), yet the cumulative curve rises 88 -> 90 -> 92. The stated justification ('small additional chances at 2028/2030') describes different Congresses that the written criterion excludes. A question with a fixed resolution date must have a flat cumulative after that date; all three horizons must be equal.

politics_us_armed_federal_state_confrontation vs politics_us_insurrection_act_invoked — CONJUNCTIVE SUBSET rated too close to its superset. The armed-confrontation event is essentially conditional on a federal deployment over gubernatorial objection. 7 against 30 implies a 23% conditional probability that such a deployment escalates to a death or a gunpoint detention between state and federal officers. Every historical analogue (1957, 1962, 1963) involved exactly that setup and resolved without a shot fired. The conditional should be 10-15% at most.

politics_coup_cluster_year — stated hazard contradicts stated cumulatives. The reasoning specifies '~35%/yr forward', which compounds to 92% by 2031 and 98.7% by 2036 versus the stated 80 and 89. The three numbers actually encode a hazard falling from ~35% to ~22% to ~18%/yr. The decaying path is the defensible one, but the stated assumption should be rewritten to match rather than left as a single rate.

politics_large_country_civil_war_onset — same defect, larger. The reasoning specifies '~25%/yr', which gives 33% by end-2027, not the stated 42%; the stated 2036 figure of 87% back-solves to ~18%/yr. The 2027 number is inconsistent with both the stated rate and the model's own outer horizons. Separately, two of the four base-rate instances (Sudan ~48m, Ukraine 44m) fall below the criterion's own 50m population floor.

politics_established_democracy_downgraded — HAZARD SHAPE inversion. 22 / 42 / 52 implies the per-report-cycle downgrade hazard is highest in the very first cycle (one report, ~22%) and then falls to roughly 2% per report-cycle in years 6-11 — below the unconditional historical base rate — while the model simultaneously asserts a record autocratization wave and a reinforcing backsliding spiral of strength 0.7. The mass is front-loaded onto the single cycle in which the strongest disconfirming evidence (a normally conducted, incumbent-losing US midterm) will already be on the record.

politics_russia_leadership_change and politics_xi_departure — FLAT-HAZARD ERROR. Both annualize a near-term mortality rate across a decade for men aged 73-74. Age-specific mortality roughly doubles between 74 and 84, so the correct 10-year cumulative is materially above the constant-rate answer. In both cases the 2027 and 2031 figures are right and only the 2036 figure is too low — the signature of this error.

politics_trump_third_term_bid — probability mass allocated to the wrong sub-window. FEC filing and state ballot-access deadlines for the 2028 cycle fall predominantly in 2027, so placing only half the total probability inside 'by 2027' implies most of the trigger mass sits in January-August 2028, when the fewest of the three listed triggers are live.

Cross-item correlation not priced. The four US institutional-rupture items (Insurrection Act 30, SCOTUS defiance 12, armed federal-state clash 7, Mexico strike 33) are treated as near-independent draws but are driven by one latent variable — the administration's willingness to convert threats into irreversible action. Thirteen months of observation across four maximal-provocation nodes with zero conversions is shared evidence against all four simultaneously, and none of the four prices it. Their implied joint 'at least one fires by 2027' is roughly 62% under independence, which is not a credible statement about a 17-month window.

politics_us_strike_inside_mexico — the criterion's resolution condition is anti-correlated with the causal pathway. It requires Mexico to publicly declare non-consent, but the modal path to a strike (US pressure producing tacit Mexican acquiescence under a 'sovereign decision' framing) is precisely the path in which Mexico does NOT so declare. The stated probability tracks P(strike), not P(strike AND public non-consent).

missing_risks.name: Contested certification of the 2028 US presidential election
missing_risks.resolution_criteria: Following the 7 November 2028 election, at least one state transmits competing slates of presidential electors to Congress, OR a state fails to certify by the Electoral Count Reform Act's safe-harbour deadline and the dispute reaches Congress or the Supreme Court, OR the joint session on 6 January 2029 sustains an objection to a state's electors.
missing_risks.reasoning: The largest omission in the model. It lists the 2028 election and the January 2027 seating as scheduled events, calls disputes over the six redrawn maps 'the most plausible near-term certification crisis', flags a certification pathway repeatedly in prose — and then encodes no discrete risk for it anywhere. This is the domain's highest-severity forcing function and the thing the entire state_of_play narrative points at. Base rate: 1 clean instance in 60 years (2020; 2000 was single-state judicial resolution without competing slates reaching the floor). The ECRA 2022 raised the objection threshold to one-fifth of each chamber and narrowed the VP's role, which cuts this materially; six states with fresh mid-decade maps, DOJ involvement in election administration, and an open Republican succession cut the other way. 14% is roughly 8x base rate for a window containing exactly one presidential cycle.

missing_risks.name: Major democratic rupture or mass communal violence in India
missing_risks.resolution_criteria: By end-2031, either (a) V-Dem downgrades India from electoral autocracy to closed autocracy, or (b) India records at least 1,000 deaths in communal, sectarian or state-repression political violence in a single calendar year per ACLED or UCDP coding, or (c) a national election is postponed beyond its constitutional deadline or its result is not accepted by the losing coalition.
missing_risks.reasoning: India is ~18% of humanity, is already coded an electoral autocracy by V-Dem, has a general election due 2029, and appears literally nowhere in this model — not in state_of_play, indicators, scheduled_events or discrete_risks. A model that names Croatia and Slovenia while omitting the world's largest electorate has a serious coverage hole, and it is exactly the hole its own structural uncertainty about 'missing backsliding where no panel is watching closely' predicts. Base rate for limb (b): Gujarat 2002 and the 1980s-90s Punjab and Kashmir insurgencies clear 1,000; roughly 3-4 such years in 40 = ~9%/yr for that limb over five years, discounted because recent episodes (Delhi 2020, Manipur 2023) have run in the hundreds rather than thousands.

missing_risks.name: Nigerian 2027 general election breakdown
missing_risks.resolution_criteria: The February 2027 Nigerian general election produces at least 500 election-related deaths within 90 days of polling per ACLED, OR the presidential result is annulled or the transfer of power prevented or delayed beyond the 29 May 2027 inauguration date, OR the military intervenes in the transfer of power.
missing_risks.reasoning: Listed as a scheduled event with the note that a disputed outcome 'would remove the main regional counterweight to Sahel juntas' — then given no probability. Nigeria is 230m people and ECOWAS's anchor, and the model's own coup-contagion feedback loop makes it the single highest-leverage node in that loop. Base rate: 2011 post-election violence killed ~800; 2019 saw ~150-300; 2023 was litigation-heavy with lower fatalities. Roughly 1 in 4 Nigerian general elections since 1999 has cleared a 500-death threshold, before adjusting up for the deteriorating northwest banditry and Sahel spillover.

missing_risks.name: Saudi succession from King Salman
missing_risks.resolution_criteria: King Salman bin Abdulaziz (b. December 1935) ceases to be King of Saudi Arabia through death, incapacity or abdication, and a successor is proclaimed, by end-2031.
missing_risks.reasoning: A SLOW-MOVING NEAR-CERTAINTY the model omits entirely. Its own structural_uncertainties section names 'the Saudi transition' as one of five correlated personalist successions, then encodes Putin, Xi and Iran as discrete risks while leaving Saudi Arabia and Kim Jong Un out. Salman turns 91 in December 2026; five-year cumulative mortality for a 90-year-old male with elite care is 75-85% before accounting for his documented decline. This is the cleanest illustration of the model's asymmetry: it prices dramatic low-probability ruptures carefully and skips high-probability structural transitions. Severity is modest because MBS is already de facto ruler and the accession is pre-arranged — but a genuinely contested outcome (severity ~8) sits at perhaps 8% of that 80%.

missing_risks.name: Global autocratization wave inflects
missing_risks.resolution_criteria: In any V-Dem Democracy Report from 2028 through 2032, either the count of countries coded as currently autocratizing falls below 35, OR the number of democratizing countries exceeds the number autocratizing; alternatively, any Freedom in the World edition through 2032 records more countries improving than declining.
missing_risks.reasoning: The model has eighteen discrete risks and every single one is a bad event. That is a framing bias the model itself identifies twice: structural_uncertainties says outright that 'the 2026 reversals may be the signal rather than the noise' and that 'a model calibrated on 2016-2025 monotone decline will systematically under-predict reversion', while feedback_loops calls electoral accountability 'the single most under-weighted loop in most pessimistic models'. Having written that, it encodes no upside-tail item. Its own continuous variables already imply this range: freedom_house_declining_countries puts a crossover at roughly p20 by 2031 and vdem_autocratizing_countries has p10 at 37. H1 2026 supplies three concrete data points — Hungary's turnover after 16 years despite a captured media environment and gerrymandered map, Starmer's removal by his own MPs, and four US executive initiatives struck down by a Court its critics called captured. A risk register with no upside tail cannot be calibrated, only conservative in one direction.

missing_risks.name: Criminal conviction of a major US opposition figure in a prosecution widely coded as politically motivated
missing_risks.resolution_criteria: By end-2031, a sitting or former US governor, senator, House member in leadership, cabinet secretary, presidential nominee, or FBI/CIA director is convicted at trial in a federal prosecution that at least three of AP/Reuters/NYT/WSJ/WaPo characterize as politically motivated or retaliatory, or that Protect Democracy's Retaliatory Action Tracker records as such.
missing_risks.reasoning: The model treats politicized prosecution as established background fact — the Comey indictment, the May 2026 SWAT raid on Virginia Senate leader Louise Lucas, Protect Democracy's tracker cited as a source, 'executive control of prosecution' named as the leading V-Dem downgrade mechanism — but encodes no discrete risk for it. This matters because it is the most likely CAUSAL PRECURSOR to the established_democracy_downgraded item and far more probable than the flashier ruptures the model does price. It is also more diagnostic than an Insurrection Act invocation for regime coding: V-Dem's Regimes-of-the-World rules weight criminalization of opposition heavily. The reason it is 26% rather than 50% is that a conviction, not an indictment, is required, and federal juries plus Article III judges have been the binding constraint — the Comey-type cases have been legally fragile.

calibration.overall_bias:
Over-forecasting drama, with a specific and diagnosable signature — but this is a good model making systematic errors, not a bad one. The bias is not uniform: it is concentrated in one cluster and reversed in another.

OVER-FORECAST CLUSTER (shrink ~0.65 toward base rate): the four US institutional-rupture items — Insurrection Act invoked (30), open SCOTUS defiance (12), armed federal-state confrontation (7), overt strike inside Mexico (33). Every one has zero-or-near-zero historical instances, every one carries a triple-digit-percent inside-view multiplier, every one is anchored on the same media-salient actor, and every one has already been at maximal hazard for thirteen months without firing. That non-firing is shared evidence against all four and is priced into none. The RN-presidency item (45 vs a $107M market at ~30-33%) belongs in the same bucket for a different reason: overriding a liquid market by 1.4x on narrative alone.

UNDER-FORECAST CLUSTER (multiply ~1.15): the slow-moving structural processes — ten-year actuarial exits for Putin and Xi (flat-hazard error), AfD in government by 2036 (discounted below its own reference class), and a NATO/EU democracy downgrade by 2036 (implied outer-year hazard below the unconditional base rate while the model asserts a record wave). The model is much better at imagining a rupture than at compounding a certainty. The omitted Saudi succession (~80% by 2031) is the purest example.

SUGGESTED GLOBAL SHRINK FACTOR: 0.80 — applied as ~0.65 to the US-rupture cluster and the French presidency, ~1.0 to the well-calibrated middle (federal-official assassination, mass-casualty attack, coup-cluster, Reform UK, Trump third term, EU exit), and ~1.15 to the actuarial and long-horizon diffusion items.

Two structural observations. First, the model is unusually honest — its contrarian_case fields repeatedly contain the correct outside view ("my 45% may be the most over-narrativized number in this set"; "the 12% may be several times too high"; "if anything, 11% by 2036 may be too high"). It writes the refutation and then does not move the number. The single highest-value process fix is mechanical: a contrarian case the analyst rates as probably correct must move the point estimate, not just the commentary.

Second, all eighteen discrete risks are negative events, despite the model arguing twice in prose that 2026 may be the peak of the wave and that electoral accountability is the most under-weighted loop in pessimistic models. It also omits India entirely — 18% of humanity, already coded an electoral autocracy — while pricing Croatia and Slovenia.
calibration.domain: Domestic political stability, governance, and social cohesion

research.state_of_play:
As of late July 2026 the global food system is in a two-track regime: physically well-supplied in aggregate, but under acute stress from three simultaneous shocks — a Middle East energy/fertilizer disruption, a Black Sea logistics collapse, and a developing strong El Niño — while the humanitarian financing that buffers the poorest has been structurally cut.

VERIFIED AGGREGATE SUPPLY. FAO's July 2026 Cereal Supply and Demand Brief puts 2026 world cereal production at 2,983 Mt, 1.9% below the 2025 all-time high but still second-largest on record; utilization 2,961 Mt; end-2027 stocks 957.8 Mt; stocks-to-use 32.0% (revised up from 31.7%). That is comfortable by historical standards — the 2007/08 crisis ratio was far lower. USDA's 10 July WASDE cut world 2026/27 wheat ending stocks to 272.8 Mt (from 275.4 Mt) and maize to 275.3 Mt (~24 Mt below last year). Rice is the standout buffer: world milled stocks hit a record 196.2 Mt entering 2026, India's stocks a record 68.4 Mt in June, India has lifted all export restrictions and targets ~30 Mt of exports, and rice export prices are roughly 35% below year-ago levels. So the "staple of the poor" is currently cheap and abundant — a materially different configuration from 2008 or 2022.

VERIFIED PRICE/SHOCK PICTURE. The FAO Food Price Index averaged 130.3 in June 2026 (-0.3% m/m, +2.2% y/y), with the cereal sub-index at 110.2 (-3.5% m/m) — i.e., benign through June. July broke that. Russia-Ukraine escalation in the Black Sea and Sea of Azov (23 strikes on Ukrainian seaports and 17 attacks on civilian vessels in the first two weeks of July; Kernel suspending its Chornomorsk terminal; Ukraine losing roughly a third of seaborne export capacity at peak harvest) pushed Chicago wheat to ~$6.80–7.00/bu, up ~16% in July and the highest since May 2024. Compounding this, USDA has US all-wheat production at 1.536 bn bu, the smallest US wheat crop in over 50 years, with hard red winter down ~41% on southern Plains drought.

VERIFIED INPUT SHOCK. The 2026 US/Israel–Iran war (began 28 Feb 2026) effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz; traffic fell >90% and remains far below the ~138 vessels/day norm (~25/day recently). Iran halted ammonia output, Qatar suspended urea/ammonia/sulfur; the World Bank estimates ~36% of traded urea and ~50% of traded sulfur were removed from the market. Urea spiked to $725.6/t in March (+53.7% m/m, four-year high); the World Bank projects the fertilizer index +31% in 2026 (urea ~+60%, MOP ~+12%, DAP up sharply on doubled sulfur). Benchmark urea was ~$435/t on 28 July, +18% m/m. Russia and China maintain fertilizer export restrictions; IFPRI's tracker reports no broad new food-export-restriction crisis yet.

VERIFIED HUNGER/HUMANITARIAN. GRFC 2026: 266 million people in IPC/CH Phase 3+ in 2025 across 47 countries (22.9% of analysed population), with 1.4 million in Phase 5 across six countries and 35.5 million children acutely malnourished. SOFI 2026 (July): 645 million hungry (7.8%), a third consecutive annual decline, and 2.1 billion moderately/severely food insecure. Sudan: famine confirmed in El Fasher and Kadugli in Sept 2025; the May 2026 IPC found no area currently in Famine but projects 200,000 in Catastrophe across 15 areas for Jun–Sep 2026, with El Fasher unreachable by road for over a year. Gaza: the 23 July 2026 IPC has the whole Strip in Phase 3 with 1.4 million in Phase 3+ through Dec 2026 and 212,000 in Phase 4 — improved post-ceasefire but aid-dependent and declining since February. WFP needs $13bn for 2026 against $6.5bn raised in 2025, faces a ~34% budget cut and a $622m six-month shortfall.

VERIFIED WATER. Indus Waters Treaty remains in abeyance (reaffirmed 3 July 2026); India rejected the 15 May 2026 Court of Arbitration award. GERD operating with no Egypt–Ethiopia agreement; Ethiopia has announced three further Blue Nile dams. Iraq had its driest year since 1933 in 2025 (reserves from ~60 BCM in 2020 to <4 BCM) with a partial winter 2025/26 reprieve and a June 2026 Iraq–Syria water MoU; Tehran reservoirs fell to ~12%. Colorado: 2007 Guidelines and 2019 DCP expire 31 Dec 2026, no seven-state deal on post-2026 rules, Reclamation advancing its own plan, Lake Mead projected to a record-low ~1,037 ft by July 2027; a two-year interim agreement was reportedly near signature in July. Counter-trend: North China Plain groundwater has been rising ~0.7 m/yr since 2020, exceeding 2005 levels by 2024.

NOT VERIFIED / INFERRED. I could not directly reach FAO, NOAA CPC, or USDA primary pages (403s). The El Niño picture — CPC advisory issued 11 June 2026, ~63% chance of a very strong peak in Nov 2026–Jan 2027 — rests on secondary sources and should be treated as directionally right but numerically soft. Claims circulating of an "18% global wheat harvest collapse" and "318 million in crisis hunger" appear on low-quality aggregator sites and are inconsistent with FAO/USDA balance sheets; I do not use them. Current Lake Mead elevation, exact Ukrainian monthly export tonnages, and the July FAO index (due ~7 Aug) are estimates.

scheduled_events.why_it_matters: First index reading capturing the July Black Sea escalation and the urea spike; a jump above ~136 would signal the benign H1 regime has ended.

scheduled_events.name: USDA August WASDE with first survey-based US corn/soybean yields
scheduled_events.why_it_matters: Resolves the biggest single uncertainty in the 2026/27 global maize balance sheet after a heat-stressed US summer and a 24 Mt y/y stock draw.

scheduled_events.why_it_matters: Determines mandatory Lower Basin cuts for 2027 and is the operative trigger for Arizona/Nevada/Mexico agricultural curtailment.

scheduled_events.why_it_matters: Without a seven-state deal or a federal Record of Decision, Colorado River operations enter legal limbo; litigation risk and Lower Basin irrigation uncertainty spike.

scheduled_events.name: Forecast peak of the 2026-27 El Nino (Nino3.4 maximum)
scheduled_events.why_it_matters: Peak-phase El Nino drives the Southern Africa maize failure window, Australian wheat drought, SE Asian rice deficits and Indian rabi/kharif anomalies for 2027.

scheduled_events.name: Southern Africa maize harvest (El Nino-exposed)
scheduled_events.why_it_matters: The 2015-16 and 2023-24 analogues each produced regional maize deficits of 20-40% and multi-million-person IPC deteriorations in Zambia, Zimbabwe, Malawi.

scheduled_events.name: Global Report on Food Crises 2027 (2026 reference year)
scheduled_events.why_it_matters: First full accounting of the effect of the 2025-26 humanitarian funding collapse on acute food insecurity headcounts.

scheduled_events.name: Indian southwest monsoon 2027 (El Nino-year)
scheduled_events.why_it_matters: El Nino years historically raise Indian deficient-monsoon odds to ~50-60%; a deficit would put India's rice and wheat export liberalisation immediately at risk.

scheduled_events.name: India general election
scheduled_events.why_it_matters: Food/fertilizer subsidy and grain export policy in India are electorally driven; pre-election periods reliably tighten export policy and expand stockholding.

scheduled_events.why_it_matters: Forcing function for reporting, financing pledges and a probable wave of replenishment conferences in 2028-2030 as the target is visibly missed.

scheduled_events.why_it_matters: Egypt and Sudan remain outside; formal operation of a basin commission without them hardens the legal split over Nile allocation.

scheduled_events.why_it_matters: Only venue with any prospect of disciplining staple export bans and the WFP humanitarian-purchase exemption.

scheduled_events.why_it_matters: Renewal negotiation with China's Lancang cascade now able to hold >20% of wet-season flow; sets data-sharing and dry-season release terms.

discrete_risks.name: New IPC/CH Famine (Phase 5) classification anywhere
discrete_risks.resolution_criteria: The IPC Famine Review Committee or a CH equivalent confirms Famine (IPC Phase 5) — with reasonable evidence or higher — for at least one geographic area not already so classified as of 2026-07-29, published on ipcinfo.org.
discrete_risks.reasoning: Sudan already has 200,000 people projected in Catastrophe across 15 areas for Jun-Sep 2026 with El Fasher road-inaccessible for over a year; WFP is running a ~34% budget cut against a $13bn requirement; Gaza's Phase 3 status is explicitly aid-dependent and coverage has fallen since February. A strong El Nino peaking Dec 2026 adds Southern Africa and Horn exposure for 2027. The binding constraint on declarations is data access, not conditions.
discrete_risks.base_rate_anchor: IPC/FRC famine confirmations: Somalia 2011, South Sudan 2017, Sudan (Zamzam) Aug 2024, Gaza Aug 2025, Sudan (El Fasher/Kadugli) Sept 2025 — 5 events in 16 years, but 3 in the last 24 months. Recent-cluster rate ~1.5/yr, long-run ~0.3/yr.
discrete_risks.contrarian_case: Declarations require survey access that is collapsing along with humanitarian budgets — conditions can worsen while confirmations fall, as happened for years in Yemen. Sudan's May 2026 analysis already de-classified active famine. A Sudan ceasefire plus continued Gaza aid flow could plausibly produce zero new confirmations through 2027 despite deteriorating reality.

discrete_risks.name: Ukrainian seaborne grain exports fall below 1 Mt in a calendar month
discrete_risks.resolution_criteria: Ukrainian Ministry of Agrarian Policy or UGA monthly data show total seaborne grain and oilseed exports below 1.0 million tonnes in any single calendar month (normal 2024-26 range ~3-5 Mt/month).
discrete_risks.reasoning: Verified: 23 strikes on Ukrainian seaports and 17 attacks on civilian vessels in the first two weeks of July 2026, with periods of zero corridor transits, Kernel suspending Chornomorsk, and about a third of seaborne capacity lost at peak harvest. Insurance withdrawal is the transmission mechanism and it moves faster than physical damage. This may already be occurring in July-August 2026 without a formal data print yet.
discrete_risks.base_rate_anchor: Since Feb 2022 Ukraine has had sub-1 Mt seaborne months in Mar-Jun 2022 and again Aug-Oct 2023 after the BSGI collapse — roughly 8 of 53 months, ~15% unconditional monthly rate, far higher conditional on active port strikes.
discrete_risks.contrarian_case: Ukraine rebuilt exports twice before under fire, via Danube ports, Romanian rail and a hugged-coast corridor, and did so within weeks. Odesa-region terminals have hardened air defence. A negotiated maritime de-escalation — which both sides have economic reasons to want during harvest — could restore flows before any month prints below 1 Mt.

discrete_risks.name: World Bank monthly urea price exceeds US$800/tonne
discrete_risks.resolution_criteria: World Bank Pink Sheet monthly average urea (Middle East, bulk, f.o.b.) exceeds US$800 per tonne in any month.
discrete_risks.reasoning: Urea already hit $725.6/t in March 2026 on Hormuz closure; Iran's ammonia is offline, Qatar suspended urea/ammonia/sulfur, ~36% of traded urea is off the market, sulfur has doubled, and the World Bank projects urea ~+60% for 2026. The war is unresolved as of late July 2026 with no active US-Iran negotiations. Only a modest further escalation is needed to clear $800.
discrete_risks.base_rate_anchor: Urea exceeded $800/t in 2008 (peak ~$770-820) and 2021-22 (peak ~$925). Roughly 2 episodes in 20 years unconditionally (~10%/yr), but conditional on an active chokepoint disruption the near-term rate is far higher.
discrete_risks.contrarian_case: Urea was $435/t on 28 July, actually below year-ago levels — the March spike was a squeeze that already unwound as Chinese and US Gulf capacity filled the gap and northern-hemisphere application season ended. Global nameplate urea capacity has expanded materially since 2022. If Hormuz partially reopens, urea could fall toward $300 and never approach $800.

discrete_risks.name: FAO Food Price Index reaches an all-time high above 160
discrete_risks.resolution_criteria: The FAO Food Price Index (2014-2016=100, nominal) monthly value exceeds 160.0, surpassing the March 2022 record of 160.3.
discrete_risks.reasoning: From 130.3 in June 2026 this requires a ~23% rise. Two simultaneous shocks (Black Sea, fertilizer) are live and a strong El Nino peaks in Dec 2026, but stocks-to-use at 32.0% and a record 196 Mt rice stockpile with India exporting freely are powerful dampers — the rice complex, which drove the 2008 spike, is currently in glut. Over longer horizons nominal drift alone (~2%/yr) closes about half the gap.
discrete_risks.base_rate_anchor: Episodes of >20% FFPI rise within 18 months: 1973-74, 2007-08, 2010-11, 2021-22 — 4 in ~52 years, ~8%/yr, with strong clustering and autocorrelation.
discrete_risks.contrarian_case: The FFPI is a nominal index in a world with 3% inflation and a weakening dollar; reaching 160 by 2031 may be near-trivial rather than a crisis signal, which argues my 2031/2036 numbers are too low. Conversely, the index is heavily weighted to vegetable oils and dairy, which are supply-elastic, so a pure cereal shock struggles to move the headline 23%.

discrete_risks.name: Two or more top-10 staple exporters impose new broad export bans/quotas simultaneously
discrete_risks.resolution_criteria: Per the IFPRI Food and Fertilizer Export Restrictions Tracker, at least two countries each ranking in the global top 10 for wheat, maize or rice exports have in force, simultaneously and for at least 60 consecutive days, a new (post-2026-07-29) export ban or quota estimated to cut that country's exports of the staple by 25% or more.
discrete_risks.reasoning: Export restrictions are the canonical amplifier: they appeared within months in 2007-08, 2010, 2022 and 2023. Russia already uses seasonal wheat quotas and export taxes; India's liberalisation is reversible in a single cabinet decision and is politically fragile in an El Nino monsoon year. The trigger is domestic price inflation, not global scarcity, which makes it fast and hard to deter.
discrete_risks.base_rate_anchor: Multi-country simultaneous staple restriction episodes: 2007-08, 2010-11, 2020 (brief, COVID), 2022-23 — 4 clusters in 20 years, each lasting 6-18 months; unconditional onset rate ~15-20%/yr but strongly conditioned on price spikes.
discrete_risks.contrarian_case: India's incentive today runs the other way — record 68.4 Mt stocks and a 30 Mt export target mean it needs to move grain, not hoard it. Russia earns hard currency from wheat under sanctions. WTO and G20 commitments plus the 2022 humanitarian-purchase exemption have raised the reputational cost. The last two years have seen restrictions unwind, not tighten.

discrete_risks.name: Animal-disease epizootic cuts a G20 country's poultry or pig inventory by 10%+ in 12 months
discrete_risks.resolution_criteria: USDA, Eurostat, WOAH or the national statistical agency of a G20 member reports a decline of 10% or more, within any rolling 12-month window, in national laying-hen inventory or national pig inventory, attributed principally to an animal disease epizootic (HPAI, ASF, FMD or successor).
discrete_risks.reasoning: H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b is now panzootic across six continents including Antarctica, with >180 million US poultry affected since 2022 and >1,000 US dairy herds infected. ASF remains entrenched in Eurasia. Layer flocks are structurally concentrated, so single-site outbreaks propagate to national inventories. This class of event now recurs roughly biennially somewhere in the G20.
discrete_risks.base_rate_anchor: Qualifying events: China ASF 2019 (pig herd -40%), US layer flock 2015 (-12%), US layer flock 2022 and again 2024-25 (~-10-13%), Japan/Korea 2020-21 poultry, EU 2021-22. Roughly 6-7 events in 12 years across the G20 ≈ 50-55%/yr.
discrete_risks.contrarian_case: Vaccination policy is shifting — France vaccinated ducks from 2023, and the US has moved toward conditional poultry vaccination — which could break the recurrence pattern within a few years. Better biosecurity and rapid depopulation have also shortened outbreak tails. My 2036 number may over-extrapolate a technology-static world.

discrete_risks.name: GRFC reports more than 300 million people in acute food insecurity
discrete_risks.resolution_criteria: Any edition of the Global Report on Food Crises published in 2027-2036 reports more than 300.0 million people in IPC/CH Phase 3 or above for its reference year.
discrete_risks.reasoning: The series ran 258m (2022), 281.6m (2023), 295.3m (2024), 266m (2025) — 300m has been approached but not crossed. Humanitarian funding is falling hard (WFP $6.5bn against a $13bn need, US share down from >33% to 15.6%) and WFP estimates cuts could push 13.7m people from Phase 3 to Phase 4. A strong El Nino peaking in Dec 2026 loads the 2027 reference year. Against this, the underlying SOFI hunger trend has fallen three years running.
discrete_risks.base_rate_anchor: In the 8-year GRFC series, the year-on-year change has exceeded +20m twice (2020, 2022) out of 7 transitions ≈ 29%/yr; from 266m a +34m jump is needed.
discrete_risks.contrarian_case: The headcount is partly an artefact of analysed-population coverage, which grew from ~1.0bn to ~1.16bn people as GRFC added countries. Coverage expansion, not deterioration, drove much of the 2020-24 rise; with assessment budgets being cut, coverage may now shrink and mechanically suppress the headline. Ceasefires in Sudan or a Ukraine settlement would each subtract tens of millions.

discrete_risks.name: World cereal production falls 4%+ year-on-year (multi-breadbasket failure)
discrete_risks.resolution_criteria: FAO's Cereal Supply and Demand Brief reports world cereal production for a calendar year at least 4.0% below the prior year's outturn (using FAO's own revised series at the time of the following year's July brief).
discrete_risks.reasoning: 2026 is already -1.9%. The developing El Nino, if it reaches very strong intensity peaking Dec 2026-Jan 2027, historically pairs with Australian wheat drought, Southern African maize failure, SE Asian rice deficits and an Indian monsoon deficit — the closest thing to a physically correlated multi-breadbasket mechanism. Compound heat-drought exposure of breadbasket regions is rising in the literature. But global cereal area and yield trends are still adding ~1%/yr, which must be overcome first.
discrete_risks.base_rate_anchor: World cereal production y/y declines of 4%+ since 1961: 1974 (-4.5%), 1983 (-5.0%), 1988 (-5.4%), and narrowly 2003 — roughly 3-4 events in 65 years ≈ 5-6%/yr, and none since 1988 as area expansion and irrigation grew.
discrete_risks.contrarian_case: The global system has not had a 4% single-year drop in nearly 40 years despite 1997-98 and 2015-16 super El Ninos; geographic diversification, irrigation, and hemispheric offsetting have made the aggregate remarkably robust. The dramatic 'simultaneous breadbasket failure' literature measures regional stress, not global production, and the two have repeatedly decoupled.

discrete_risks.name: World cereal stocks-to-use ratio falls below 28%
discrete_risks.resolution_criteria: FAO's Cereal Supply and Demand Brief reports a world cereal stocks-to-use ratio below 28.0% for any marketing year.
discrete_risks.reasoning: Current ratio is 32.0%, revised up. FAO regards below ~30% as tight and the series low on the current methodology is around 29% (2007/08). Getting to 28% requires either a large production shortfall or sustained stock drawdown, most plausibly via China releasing or reclassifying reserves. USDA already shows maize stocks down ~24 Mt y/y, so the direction is right but the level has far to fall.
discrete_risks.base_rate_anchor: On FAO's current series, the ratio has been below 28% in zero of the last 25 years; the 2007/08 crisis trough was ~29%. Two-consecutive-year drawdowns of >2 points occurred in 2002-03, 2006-07 and 2012-13 — ~3 in 25 years.
discrete_risks.contrarian_case: China holds well over half of reported world wheat and maize stocks, and those are largely inaccessible to world trade. The effective ex-China ratio is already far below 28%, meaning the headline metric may simply be the wrong instrument — the risk could materialise as a price crisis with the headline ratio unchanged, making this event both understated as a signal and overstated as a threshold.

discrete_risks.name: Thai 5% broken rice benchmark exceeds US$650/tonne
discrete_risks.resolution_criteria: FAO GIEWS / Thai Rice Exporters Association monthly average f.o.b. price for Thai white rice 5% broken exceeds US$650 per tonne.
discrete_risks.reasoning: Rice is the single most reassuring number in the current dataset: record 196.2 Mt world stocks, record 68.4 Mt Indian stocks, India exporting without restriction and targeting 30 Mt, prices ~35% off. A move to $650 requires both a large Asian production shock (El Nino is the plausible mechanism for 2027) and an Indian export reversal. Both are needed; neither alone suffices given the stock overhang.
discrete_risks.base_rate_anchor: Thai 5% has exceeded $650/t in 2008 (peak ~$1,000) and briefly 2023-24 (~$650) — 2 episodes in 20 years ≈ 10%/yr, both triggered by Indian export bans rather than by production alone.
discrete_risks.contrarian_case: The 2023 episode showed how fast this can flip: India banned non-basmati white rice exports in July 2023 and Thai prices rose ~50% within four months from an equally comfortable-looking stock position. Political triggers can outrun physical buffers, so my 2027 number of 9% may be too low if the 2027 monsoon disappoints.

discrete_risks.name: India physically curtails Indus western-river flows to Pakistan
discrete_risks.resolution_criteria: Pakistan's IRSA rim-station data, corroborated by satellite/independent hydrological analysis, show a sustained reduction of 20% or more over at least four consecutive weeks in Chenab or Jhelum inflows attributable to Indian storage operations or diversion, and not to natural hydrology.
discrete_risks.reasoning: The Treaty has been in abeyance since April 2025, reaffirmed 3 July 2026, and India rejected the 15 May 2026 Court of Arbitration award as null. Reservoir flushing at Baglihar and Salal in 2025 produced short flow perturbations already. India has publicly accelerated storage and diversion planning. The constraint is physical: India currently has only ~1 MAF of live storage on the western rivers against ~135 MAF of flow, and building meaningful storage or the Chenab-Ravi link takes 5-12 years — which is exactly why the risk rises steeply toward 2036.
discrete_risks.base_rate_anchor: In 65 years the Treaty survived three wars and Kargil with zero deliberate flow curtailment — an unconditional base rate near zero. But the treaty-in-abeyance regime has only existed for 15 months, so the reference class is now 'unilateral riparian abrogation with construction underway,' which historically resolves into curtailment in a substantial minority of cases (Turkey-Euphrates 1990, Israel-Jordan pre-1994).
discrete_risks.contrarian_case: India gains little and risks enormously: curtailment would be an unambiguous casus belli against a nuclear state, would set a precedent China could apply to the Brahmaputra, and would flood Indian Kashmir if storage were operated aggressively. 'Abeyance' has so far been legal signalling with almost no hydrological content, and may remain so indefinitely — the cheapest option for Delhi is to keep the threat rather than exercise it.

discrete_risks.name: Armed attack on GERD or an Egypt-Ethiopia armed clash over Nile water
discrete_risks.resolution_criteria: ACLED or equivalent records a state-attributed kinetic attack (air, missile, drone or special-forces) on the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam or associated Ethiopian water infrastructure, or a direct armed exchange between Egyptian and Ethiopian forces publicly framed by either government as arising from the Nile water dispute.
discrete_risks.reasoning: Egypt has made explicit existential rhetoric for 15 years, GERD was inaugurated in Sept 2025 with no agreement, and Ethiopia announced three further Blue Nile dams in 2026 — each new dam is a fresh escalation point. Egypt has also drawn closer to Somalia and Eritrea, giving it proxy options. But the dam is now full and operating: destroying it would create a catastrophic flood wave onto Sudan and Egypt itself, which inverts the military logic.
discrete_risks.base_rate_anchor: Interstate armed attacks specifically over shared water infrastructure since 1945 are extremely rare — Israel-Syria 1965-67 headwater diversion clashes, Israel's 1981 and 2007 strikes were on nuclear not water targets. Roughly 1-2 clear cases in 80 years. Loaded rhetoric is a very weak predictor of strikes.
discrete_risks.contrarian_case: The strongest counter to my low number: Egypt's leverage window is closing permanently as GERD normalises, and Egypt is simultaneously facing Nile flow limits with 98% freshwater dependence and a fast-growing population. Leaders facing irreversible loss sometimes act late and badly. Also, a strike on a construction-phase new dam is militarily far cheaper than one on GERD itself.

discrete_risks.name: Colorado River enters 2027 without an agreed post-2026 framework
discrete_risks.resolution_criteria: On 1 January 2027, no seven-state consensus agreement and no signed federal Record of Decision governs Lake Powell/Lake Mead operations for calendar 2027, with operations instead running under an interim stopgap, unilateral federal action, or litigation.
discrete_risks.reasoning: Verified as of July 2026: the 2007 Guidelines and 2019 DCP expire 31 December 2026, the seven states still have no consensus, Reclamation released a Draft EIS in January 2026 and is proceeding with its own plan, and a two-year interim agreement was only 'set to be signed' as of late July. The interim deal, if signed, is itself a stopgap rather than the post-2026 framework — so partial resolution is the modal outcome. Note this risk is near-binary in 2027 and barely moves afterward, since by 2031 something will govern operations.
discrete_risks.base_rate_anchor: Colorado River negotiations have missed federal deadlines repeatedly: the 2023 consensus deadline slipped, the March 2024 and November 2024 milestones both slipped, and the 2025 deadline produced no Upper/Lower Basin agreement. 4-5 missed deadlines in 4 years.
discrete_risks.contrarian_case: An 8NewsNow report in July 2026 says the states are on the verge of signing a two-year deal, and Metropolitan Water District and IID have both inked large conservation agreements. If the interim deal is signed and a ROD issues in the autumn, this resolves NO and my 45% is roughly double what it should be. The parties have also never actually let operations fall into litigation.

discrete_risks.name: WFP annual contributions fall below US$5 billion
discrete_risks.resolution_criteria: WFP's published annual contribution total for any calendar year 2026-2036 is below US$5.0 billion (nominal), per wfp.org contributions data.
discrete_risks.reasoning: Verified trajectory: $9.8bn (2022) to $8.3bn (2023) to ~$9.8bn peak then $6.5bn (2025) against a $13bn 2026 requirement, with a ~34% budget cut and the US share falling from over a third to 15.6% after USAID's dismantlement and an upheld $8bn congressional rescission. Two more years of the same slope lands below $5bn. European fiscal consolidation and defence reallocation point the same way.
discrete_risks.base_rate_anchor: WFP contributions fell year-on-year in 2016, 2023, 2024 and 2025 — 4 of the last 12 years, but the last three are consecutive and driven by a structural donor-base change, not cyclical variation.
discrete_risks.contrarian_case: Famine imagery has historically reversed donor retrenchment sharply and quickly — 2011 Somalia and 2017 quadruple-famine appeal both produced step-changes in funding. Gulf donors, China and philanthropic capital are partially substituting. And a US administration change in Jan 2029 could restore a large share of the cut within one budget cycle.

discrete_risks.name: Highly virulent wheat rust or blast establishes in the Indian/Pakistani Punjab
discrete_risks.resolution_criteria: CIMMYT, BGRI, FAO or a national plant protection agency confirms establishment of a Ug99-lineage stem rust race, a novel highly virulent stripe rust race defeating deployed resistance, or wheat blast (Magnaporthe oryzae Triticum), in Indian or Pakistani Punjab or Haryana, with documented field-scale infection.
discrete_risks.reasoning: Ug99 emerged in Uganda in 1998 and reached Iran by 2007 — one wind-corridor step from South Asia — then stalled there for nearly 20 years. Wheat blast, however, jumped from South America to Bangladesh in 2016 and Zambia in 2018, demonstrating that seed-borne long-distance introduction works. The Indo-Gangetic Plain is ~100 Mt of wheat on a narrow resistance base, and warming expands the rust-favourable window.
discrete_risks.base_rate_anchor: Major transcontinental establishment of a wheat pathogen in a new mega-region: Ug99 into Yemen/Iran (2006-07), stripe rust race Yr27 across South/West Asia (2009-10), wheat blast into Bangladesh (2016) and Zambia (2018) — roughly 4 events in 20 years globally, of which ~1 landed in South Asia.
discrete_risks.contrarian_case: Two decades of BGRI/DRRW surveillance and pre-emptive breeding have deployed Sr2-complex and multi-gene resistance across most South Asian mega-varieties, and India rotates cultivars faster than in the 1960s. The 2036 number could reasonably be half what I give. Conversely, if surveillance funding follows aid funding downward, detection lags could make it look like a sudden emergence.

discrete_risks.name: Three or more countries/territories in confirmed IPC Famine simultaneously
discrete_risks.resolution_criteria: At any point in a calendar year, IPC/FRC-confirmed Famine (Phase 5) classifications are simultaneously in force for areas in three or more distinct countries or territories.
discrete_risks.reasoning: 2025 was the first year with two concurrent famine confirmations (Gaza and Sudan) in IPC history. The candidate set for a third is real — Haiti, Mali, South Sudan and Yemen all had Phase 5 populations in 2025, and Afghanistan and Syria are deteriorating. The funding cut is the common cause that could correlate these. But confirmation requires all three IPC famine thresholds plus survey access in three places at once, which is a high bar.
discrete_risks.base_rate_anchor: Concurrent confirmed famines: 0 instances in 2004-2023, 1 instance (2 countries) in 2025. Never 3. Reference class of 'multiple concurrent famines' has one observation in 20 years.
discrete_risks.contrarian_case: Three simultaneous confirmations may be institutionally near-impossible rather than merely unlikely — FRC processes are slow, politically contested (Israel and Sudan both disputed their classifications), and resource-constrained. The failure mode is under-declaration. My 2036 figure of 34% could be double the truth for the resolvable event even if the underlying reality is worse.

discrete_risks.name: Hormuz fertilizer flows normalise (downside-risk-off event)
discrete_risks.resolution_criteria: World Bank or IFA data show Middle East seaborne urea and ammonia export volumes recovering to 90% or more of their 2024-25 monthly average for three consecutive months.
discrete_risks.reasoning: Included deliberately as the balancing counterpart to the fertilizer spike risk. As of 27 July 2026 the US has paused strikes, Iran-Oman talks on Strait transit are underway, and traffic has partially recovered (25 vessels/day from a near-total stop). Both belligerents and every Gulf producer have strong economic incentives to restore flows; Qatari and Saudi plants are repairable in months, and Iranian ammonia restarts quickly once gas and shipping resume.
discrete_risks.base_rate_anchor: Chokepoint closures historically resolve fast: Suez 1967-75 is the outlier; Bab el-Mandeb Houthi disruption (2023-25) never fully closed, Hormuz tanker war 1984-88 saw traffic continue throughout at reduced rates. Median major chokepoint disruption duration is well under 24 months.
discrete_risks.contrarian_case: Iran has stated it wants a new transit regime with tolls, i.e. a permanently altered rather than restored status quo. If Iran institutionalises partial control, 'normalisation' to 90% of prior volumes may never resolve YES even with peace — flows would reroute permanently to non-Gulf suppliers and Middle East export share would fall structurally.

continuous_variables.name: FAO Food Price Index (nominal)
continuous_variables.notes: June 2026 verified value; July will print materially higher on Black Sea escalation. Drift ~2%/yr nominal reflects general inflation plus modest real softening; vol calibrated to the 1990-2025 monthly series (~9% annualised) with a fat right tail for crisis years. p90 of 198 exceeds the March 2022 record of 160.3, consistent with a ~40% chance of an all-time high by 2031.

continuous_variables.name: World cereal stocks-to-use ratio
continuous_variables.notes: FAO July 2026 brief, verified. Strongly mean-reverting via price-induced supply response, so the effective sigma over 5.4 years (~2.7 pts) is well below the random-walk value (~3.5 pts). Note that over half of reported stocks are Chinese and not tradeable, so the ex-China ratio is roughly 18-20% and far more volatile.

continuous_variables.name: World cereal production
continuous_variables.notes: FAO July 2026 forecast, verified (-1.9% vs 2025 record). Drift ~0.9%/yr reflects yield trend net of decelerating area expansion and warming drag. Vol from the 1961-2025 detrended residual series (~2% of level). Left tail should be modelled with negative skew and ENSO-conditional correlation across breadbaskets.

continuous_variables.name: Urea price (Middle East granular, f.o.b.)
continuous_variables.notes: Current value is a 2026 blended estimate: benchmark spot was $435/t on 28 July but the Middle East series peaked at $725.6/t in March; use ~$520 as the year-average anchor. Drift and vol are LOG (fractional) — negative drift encodes post-shock mean reversion toward the ~$350 marginal-cost band as Gulf and US Gulf Coast capacity returns. Strongly gas-price-coupled: correlate with TTF/Henry Hub.

continuous_variables.name: People in acute food insecurity (IPC/CH Phase 3+, GRFC)
continuous_variables.notes: GRFC 2026 verified value for reference year 2025. Drift is modestly positive: humanitarian funding contraction and conflict persistence push up, while the underlying SOFI hunger trend pushes down. Vol reflects observed year-on-year swings of +/- 20-35m. Caution: the analysed population is itself a moving denominator, adding ~10m of pure measurement noise.

continuous_variables.name: People in IPC/CH Phase 5 (Catastrophe)
continuous_variables.notes: GRFC 2026 verified (2025 reference year, 6 countries). Highly right-skewed and effectively floored near zero; model as a lognormal or compound-Poisson with famine-event jumps rather than a Gaussian random walk. Sudan alone accounts for a large share and is bimodal on ceasefire/no-ceasefire.

continuous_variables.name: CBOT front-month wheat price
continuous_variables.notes: Verified late-July 2026 level, a two-year high. Drift and vol are LOG. Left tail is bounded near ~$4.50 by North American and Black Sea cash costs of production; right tail is fat (2008 peak $13, 2022 peak $13.6). Correlate strongly with urea (input cost pass-through, ~0.4) and with Black Sea conflict indicators.

continuous_variables.name: Thai white rice 5% broken, f.o.b.
continuous_variables.notes: Currently depressed ~35% on record 196.2 Mt world stocks and India's full export liberalisation. Drift/vol are LOG. The distribution is strongly regime-dependent rather than continuous: an Indian export ban is a discrete jump of +40-60% within months, so pair this variable with foodwater_new_staple_export_bans rather than modelling it as pure diffusion.

continuous_variables.name: Lake Mead elevation
continuous_variables.notes: Current value is INFERRED (Reclamation's July 2026 24-Month Study projects 1,037 ft by July 2027, verified). Negative drift reflects structural over-allocation of ~1.2-1.5 MAF/yr against a declining flow trend. Hard floors: 1,000 ft (Hoover minimum power pool ~950; deadpool ~895). Anti-correlated with El Nino in the Lower Basin, which typically brings wet Southwest winters.

continuous_variables.name: WFP annual contributions received
continuous_variables.notes: 2025 verified against a stated $13bn 2026 requirement. Drift encodes the structural US withdrawal (share fell from >33% to 15.6%) partially offset by Gulf and EU substitution. Vol reflects appeal-driven spikes. Should be modelled with a regime switch on US administration change in Jan 2029.

continuous_variables.name: Global undernourishment headcount (PoU)
continuous_variables.notes: SOFI 2026 verified (7.8% of world population, third consecutive decline). Drift continues the recent improvement but at a decaying rate; the SDG2 2030 target is unreachable. Note the PoU is a modelled series revised retroactively by several tens of millions, so real-time uncertainty exceeds the stated vol.

continuous_variables.name: Share of marine fish stocks within biologically sustainable levels
continuous_variables.notes: FAO SOFIA 2026 verified, down from 64.5%. FAO notes part of the fall is methodological (new stocks added), so drift is uncertain in sign for well-managed regions — North Atlantic and NE Pacific stocks are improving while Mediterranean, SE Asian and West African stocks decline. Reported only biennially, so the simulation should hold the value flat between SOFIA editions.

feedback_loops.name: Export-restriction cascade
feedback_loops.mechanism: A price rise raises domestic food inflation in exporting countries; governments impose bans or quotas to protect consumers; the withdrawn volume tightens the thin world market further, raising prices and triggering the next country. Importers respond with panic procurement and stock-building, amplifying again. This loop, not physical scarcity, converted a modest 2007-08 rice deficit into a tripling of prices and did the same in 2023.

feedback_loops.name: Price-induced supply response
feedback_loops.mechanism: High grain prices raise expected margins, so farmers expand planted area, apply more fertilizer, and shift toward the high-priced crop; northern and southern hemisphere plantings give two shots per year. Global cereal area and yield respond with an elasticity of roughly 0.1-0.2 within two seasons. This is the single most reliable damper in the system and is why 4%+ global production drops have not occurred since 1988.

feedback_loops.name: Stock buffer nonlinearity
feedback_loops.mechanism: Held stocks absorb production shortfalls with little price movement while the stocks-to-use ratio is above ~30%, but price sensitivity to a given shortfall rises hyperbolically as the ratio falls below ~25%. The buffer is therefore a damper that fails abruptly rather than gradually — and because over half of reported world stocks sit in China and are not tradeable, the effective buffer is far smaller than the headline 32.0% implies.

feedback_loops.name: Fertilizer-price to yield-erosion loop
feedback_loops.mechanism: An energy or chokepoint shock raises ammonia and urea costs; smallholders and margin-constrained farmers cut application rates; nitrogen-limited yields fall one to two seasons later, especially in sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia; the resulting grain tightness raises crop prices, which sustains fertilizer demand and prices. The 2021-22 shock is estimated to have cost sub-Saharan African maize yields several percent in 2022-23 via exactly this channel.

feedback_loops.name: Aid-funding to hunger to instability loop
feedback_loops.mechanism: Falling humanitarian budgets reduce food transfers; acute malnutrition and displacement rise; displacement and grievance feed conflict recruitment and disrupt planting and market access; conflict raises the caseload, which raises the appeal, which is met at a lower coverage ratio. WFP's own estimate that cuts could push 13.7 million people from Phase 3 to Phase 4 is the first turn of this loop.

feedback_loops.name: Demand-side substitution valve
feedback_loops.mechanism: Roughly 40% of world maize goes to animal feed and ~10% to ethanol. When grain prices spike, feed rations shift toward wheat, byproducts and oilseed meal, ethanol blending economics deteriorate and mandates get waived, and livestock herds are liquidated. This releases large volumes back to food use within a single season — a much faster elastic margin than supply expansion.

feedback_loops.name: Logistics rerouting under interdiction
feedback_loops.mechanism: When a corridor is interdicted, trade reroutes: Ukraine shifted to Danube barges, Romanian and Polish rail and a hugged-coast Black Sea route within weeks in both 2022 and 2023; Hormuz fertilizer flows are being partially substituted by Chinese, North African and US Gulf Coast supply. Rerouting raises freight costs by 20-60% but restores most volume, capping the duration of chokepoint shocks well below their initial headline severity.

feedback_loops.name: Groundwater depletion and the efficiency trap
feedback_loops.mechanism: Falling water tables raise pumping energy costs; farmers respond by installing drip and sprinkler systems, but because subsidised efficiency raises returns per unit water they expand irrigated area or shift to thirstier high-value crops, so basin-scale consumptive use rises rather than falls. Documented in the Indian Punjab, the Ogallala and the Guadiana. The North China Plain's post-2020 recovery of ~0.7 m/yr is the counter-example, achieved only via massive inter-basin transfer plus enforced pumping caps.

feedback_loops.name: Adaptation and breeding vs climate yield drag
feedback_loops.mechanism: Warming and compound heat-drought erode potential yields, but cultivar turnover, heat-escape sowing dates, expanded irrigation and increasingly genomic selection and gene editing have so far offset the drag, keeping global yield trends near +1%/yr. Whether this stays balancing depends on sustained CGIAR and national R&D funding, which is currently falling alongside humanitarian budgets.

structural_uncertainties: Chinese stock opacity. China is reported to hold roughly half of world wheat and over 60% of world maize stocks. The headline 32.0% stocks-to-use ratio, which is the model's main comfort signal, may be materially overstated as a global buffer — the tradeable ex-China ratio is closer to 18-20%. If Chinese reserves are also smaller or lower-quality than reported, the entire price-response function of this model is miscalibrated and shocks would transmit far more violently than simulated.

Measurement regime change in hunger statistics. The GRFC headcount depends on an analysed population that has grown from ~1.0bn to ~1.16bn people, and IPC/CH assessments are themselves funded by the same donors now cutting budgets. Hunger could rise while measured hunger falls, or vice versa. Any risk defined on a published IPC number is partly a forecast of surveillance capacity, not of the world.

Yield-trend regime break in either direction. The model assumes ~+0.9%/yr global cereal production growth. Gene editing, hybrid wheat, AI-accelerated breeding and biologicals could plausibly push this to 1.5-2%/yr by the 2030s and make most scarcity risks obsolete; alternatively a step-change in compound heat-drought frequency over the Indo-Gangetic Plain, North China Plain and Central Europe, plus stagnating R&D funding, could flatten it to near zero. These branches diverge by 300+ Mt by 2036 and I cannot distinguish them.

Fast geopolitical resolution. Two of the three live shocks — the Black Sea interdiction and the Hormuz closure — could each end within months of a political decision. A Ukraine settlement plus a US-Iran deal would simultaneously restore ~40 Mt of grain exports and ~36% of traded urea, collapsing most of the near-term risk distribution. My probabilities implicitly assume grinding continuation, which is the modal but not dominant path.

Correlated-shock structure is under-modelled. I treat breadbasket outcomes as weakly correlated, but ENSO teleconnections and persistent jet-stream wave patterns can synchronise failures across the Northern Hemisphere mid-latitudes in ways historical covariance matrices understate. If the true correlation in a strong El Nino year is 0.5 rather than 0.2, multi-breadbasket failure probability is roughly double what I state.

Transboundary hydrological data is politically produced. Indus rim-station flows, Nile releases from GERD, and Lancang-Mekong dam operations are all reported by parties with an interest in the number. Several of my water risks are defined on data the interested party controls, so they may be unresolvable or resolvable falsely. Satellite altimetry and gravimetry partially substitute but with months of lag.

Demand-side technology shock. Sustained GLP-1 uptake, cultivated and fermentation-derived protein, and continued Chinese pork demand decline could reduce feed-grain demand growth by 0.5-1%/yr by the mid-2030s — enough to make the entire scarcity framing of this domain wrong on the 10-year horizon while leaving the distributional and famine risks, which are about conflict and money rather than calories, completely unchanged.

Fertilizer-energy decoupling. Green ammonia at scale, US shale-gas-based capacity expansion, and precision-agriculture nitrogen reduction could sever the gas-fertilizer-food price chain that drives several of my risks. Conversely, a carbon price on ammonia without substitutes available would tighten it further. I have no confident view on which dominates by 2031.

adjustments.justification: COHERENCE (fixed-date event) + BASE RATE. The resolution criterion is evaluated at a single instant — 1 January 2027 — so the event is fully resolved before 2027 ends.
