Assigning 45/48/50 across three horizons is structurally impossible: no additional probability can accrue after the resolution date. All three cells must be identical. Separately the level is too high: the criterion resolves YES only if there is BOTH no seven-state consensus AND no signed federal ROD. Reclamation's published Post-2026 NEPA schedule targets a Record of Decision by 1 October 2026, with the Draft EIS already out (comment period closed 2 March 2026) and a Lower Basin three-state proposal filed May 2026 with conservation plans due August 2026. A ROD is the modal federal outcome precisely because operations legally cannot be undefined. P(no consensus AND no ROD by 1 Jan 2027) is closer to 30-35%.
Same fixed-date coherence defect: the event resolves on 1 Jan 2027 and cannot gain probability by 2036. Must equal the 2027 value.

Level correction as above — the criterion's 'or a signed federal ROD' escape hatch is the modal path, and Reclamation is driving to it on a published Oct 2026 timeline. The analyst's own contrarian case says 45 is 'roughly double what it should be'; 32 splits the difference while preserving real slippage risk given 4-5 missed deadlines in 4 years.

COHERENCE with own continuous variable. By end-2027 only one edition (GRFC 2027, 2026 reference year) can resolve this. The model's own acute_food_insecure variable has current_value 266, annual_drift +4.5, annual_vol 21. A single one-year-ahead draw exceeding 300 requires (300-270.5)/21 = 1.40 sigma, i.e. ~8%. Even generously loading El Nino and the aid cut into the drift (say +12), it is ~12-15%. 38% is roughly 3-4x the model's own stated distribution. Note also the series has never crossed 300 in 8 editions and just fell 29m.

UNDER-forecast on the long horizon relative to the same continuous variable. By 2031 there are five independent-ish annual draws; p50_2031 = 290 and p90 = 356. The running maximum over five draws around a mean rising from ~270 to 290 with sd 21 exceeds 300 with probability ~70-75%. The near-term number was too high and the medium-term too low — the hazard shape is inverted.

Same running-maximum logic over ten draws with positive drift; by the mid-2030s the model's own median path is at or above 300, so the probability of ever printing >300 in one of ten editions should be mid-80s. Only a coverage contraction (fewer analysed countries) argues it down, and that is already priced by not going to 92.

BASE RATE + internal inconsistency with own vol parameter. world_cereal_production has annual_drift +26 Mt and annual_vol 62 Mt. A 4% y/y fall from ~3,050 Mt is -122 Mt; against trend that is a -148 Mt shock = 2.4 sigma = ~0.8%/yr, or ~4% over 5.4 years. The historical base rate is more generous (3-4 events in 65 years = 5%/yr, giving ~24% by 2031) but the analyst themselves note zero events in 38 years, implying a modern rate nearer 2.5%/yr = 13%. 31% sits above even the raw historical rate while the mechanism (single strong El Nino) has twice — 1997-98 and 2015-16 — failed to produce one. 18% is a generous blend that already prices rising breadbasket correlation.

Same reasoning extended: even the unconditional 5%/yr historical rate gives 41% by 2036, and the post-1988 record plus the analyst's own 'price-induced supply response' damper (strength 0.85) argues for materially less. 47% implies a per-year hazard around 6%, i.e. that the next decade is more shock-prone than the 1970s-80s despite irrigation, hemispheric offsetting and a 0.9%/yr trend that must be overcome first.

UNDER-forecast, and inconsistent with own continuous variable. The note claims p90_2031=198 is 'consistent with ~40% chance of an all-time high by 2031' — that conflates terminal-value exceedance with the running maximum of a MONTHLY series over 5.4 years. With p50_2031=146 and a right tail to 198, the chance that at least one monthly print in 65 months touches 160.2 is ~55-65%, not 42%. Nominal drift of 2.8%/yr alone carries the median to ~152 by 2031 with ~12%/yr vol around it.

HAZARD SHAPE / nominal-threshold error. At the model's own 2.8%/yr drift, the median FFPI is ~168 by 2036 — above the 160.2 threshold. When the median path crosses the barrier, P(ever crossing) should be well above 50%, not 60%. This is a nominal index against a fixed nominal barrier; the analyst flags this in their own contrarian case ('reaching 160 by 2031 may be near-trivial') and then does not act on it. 82% is the honest number for a monthly running max.

UNDER-forecast against the analyst's OWN base rate. They state 6-7 qualifying events in 12 years across the G20 = 50-55%/yr, i.e. lambda ~0.7/yr. Poisson over 5.4 years gives 1-exp(-3.8) = 98%. Even halving the rate for vaccination progress (France ducks 2023, US conditional poultry vaccination) gives 87%. The criterion is also very broad — ANY G20 member, laying-hen OR pig inventory, 10% over any rolling 12-month window, HPAI/ASF/FMD/successor. The US layer flock alone has cleared 10% in 2015, 2022 and 2024-25. 90% is conservative.

Same: lambda 0.7/yr over 1.42 years gives 63%; the current H5N1 panzootic state and entrenched Eurasian ASF argue for at or above the base rate, not below it. 58% allows for vaccination-driven attenuation already beginning.

Ten years at even a heavily attenuated 0.35/yr hazard gives 97%. 87% implies the recurrence pattern essentially stops within a few years, which the contrarian case raises as a possibility but cannot support at that strength for a criterion this broad across 19 G20 members and two species.

BASE RATE inflated by availability. Original 44%. Spot urea was $435/t on 28 July 2026, BELOW year-ago levels — the March squeeze to $725.6 already unwound as Chinese and US Gulf capacity filled in. Clearing $800 as a MONTHLY World Bank average requires +84% from spot, i.e. a spike larger than the one Hormuz closure itself produced. Unconditional base rate is 2 episodes in 20 years (~10%/yr). There is also tension with the model's own 58% probability that Hormuz fertilizer flows normalise by 2027: the two are near-complementary in practice, and the analyst gives them 44+58 = 102 without acknowledging the near-exclusivity.

Same overweighting of a spike that has already unwound, plus material nameplate capacity expansion since 2022 and negative log drift in their own urea continuous variable (-3%/yr toward the ~$350 marginal-cost band). Their own p90_2031 for urea is $852 — a single-year terminal p90, which over five years of running maxima supports roughly 40-50%, not 58%.

Modest trim only. The long horizon is partly rescued by nominal inflation: $800 in 2036 is ~$620 in 2026 dollars, a threshold urea already exceeded in 2022 and nearly in March 2026. This is the one horizon where the original number is close to defensible, so the revision is small.

UNDER-forecast against their own base rate. They state 4 clusters in 20 years and an unconditional onset rate of 15-20%/yr. At 18%/yr, P by 2031 (5.4 yr) = 65%. Their 2027 figure of 26% is internally consistent with ~18%/yr, but the 2031 figure implies the hazard falls to ~12%/yr after 2027 for no stated reason. The criterion is also broad — any two top-10 exporters of ANY of wheat, maize or rice, 25% export cut, 60 days.

HAZARD SHAPE. At a constant 18%/yr the 2036 value is 88%; at a decayed 12%/yr it is 74%. 68% implies a per-year hazard falling to ~8%/yr in the 2030s, i.e. that the 2007-08 / 2010-11 / 2020 / 2022-23 pattern of roughly one cluster every 5 years stops. Nothing in the model supports that; the export-restriction cascade loop is rated 0.75 reinforcing.

SCOPE + base rate. As of the May 2026 IPC, ZERO areas are in confirmed Famine. Reaching three simultaneous confirmations in three distinct countries within 17 months requires three independent FRC processes to complete and overlap in time from a standing start. Concurrent confirmed famines have one observation (2 countries, 2025) in 20+ years, and the failure mode of the system under budget cuts is under-declaration, not over-declaration. 10% is roughly double.

The reference class has exactly one observation and it was for two, not three, countries. FRC confirmations are slow, survey-access-bound and politically contested (both Israel and Sudan disputed theirs), and IPC assessment budgets are funded by the same donors cutting WFP. The analyst's own contrarian case says three concurrent may be 'institutionally near-impossible rather than merely unlikely' and that the number could be double the truth — I agree and act on it.
Same, scaled. Retains a real rising trend (three of five historical confirmations came in the last 24 months) without extrapolating a one-observation reference class into a one-in-three decade event.

BASE RATE + physical constraint the analyst themselves state. India has ~1 MAF of live storage against ~135 MAF of western-river flow; a sustained 20% cut to Chenab or Jhelum for four consecutive weeks is not physically deliverable with run-of-river infrastructure outside brief low-flow reservoir-flushing windows, and the Chenab-Ravi link plus new storage takes 5-12 years. 65 years and three wars produced zero curtailment. 24% by 2031 prices too much of the 2036 story into the 2031 cell; the escalating-toward-2036 shape is right but the level in the middle horizon is not.

By end-2027 essentially no new Indian storage will be commissioned, so the only mechanism is reservoir flushing/filling at Baglihar and Salal, which historically produced perturbations of days, not four sustained weeks at -20%. The criterion also requires attribution net of natural hydrology corroborated by independent analysis — a high evidentiary bar on data the interested parties control (a point the model raises in its own structural uncertainties but does not price).

UNDER-forecast on the long horizon. Base rate is 2 episodes in 20 years (~10%/yr), which over 10.4 years gives 66%; the current rice glut is a 2026-28 fact, not a 2030s fact, and cannot justify halving the hazard for a full decade. Nominal drift also erodes the fixed $650 barrier. Both prior episodes were triggered by a single Indian cabinet decision, which is a fast-recurring political hazard rather than a slow physical one.

Small trim. The declaration hazard is genuinely high (recent-cluster rate ~1.5/yr), but the analyst identifies the binding constraint as survey access and then does not discount for it — the May 2026 Sudan analysis found NO area currently in Famine despite worse conditions, which is exactly the under-declaration failure mode. Blending the recent-cluster rate (1.5/yr, giving 88%) with the long-run rate (0.3/yr, giving 35%) at 70/30 weight gives ~72%; discounting for collapsing assessment funding lands at ~68%. 2031 (93) and 2036 (97) are defensible and left alone.

HAZARD SHAPE. Going 62 to 70 to 74 implies that if no sub-1 Mt month occurs by end-2027, the residual hazard collapses to ~2%/yr. That is too sharp even assuming a Ukraine settlement: the base rate of 8 sub-1 Mt months in 53 war months reflects one conflict, but Black Sea port infrastructure remains a standing target class, and a decade is long enough for renewed interdiction, a Kerch/Danube disruption, or a harvest failure. Raise 2031 to 78 and, implicitly, 2036 toward 82.

coherence_violations: FIXED-DATE EVENT GIVEN A RISING PROBABILITY CURVE. foodwater_colorado_no_deal resolves on a single instant — 1 January 2027 — yet is given 45 / 48 / 50 across 2027/2031/2036. A date-fixed event cannot accrue probability after its resolution date. All three cells must be identical. The analyst even notes 'this risk is near-binary in 2027 and barely moves afterward' and then moves it anyway.

DISCRETE RISK CONTRADICTS ITS OWN CONTINUOUS VARIABLE (GRFC). foodwater_grfc_above_300m puts 38% on a single one-year-ahead draw exceeding 300m, while acute_food_insecure specifies current 266, drift +4.5, vol 21 — implying (300-270.5)/21 = 1.40 sigma = ~8%. The discrete number is 3-4x the model's own stated distribution.

DISCRETE RISK CONTRADICTS ITS OWN CONTINUOUS VARIABLE (CEREAL PRODUCTION). foodwater_global_cereal_drop_4pct assigns 31%/47%, but world_cereal_production specifies annual_vol 62 Mt against +26 Mt drift, making a 4% (~-122 Mt) y/y fall a ~2.4-sigma event, i.e. <1%/yr, or ~5% by 2031. The stated p10_2031 of 2,955 Mt (barely below today's 2,983) is also inconsistent with a 31% chance of a single-year 4% collapse somewhere in the interval.

RUNNING-MAXIMUM vs TERMINAL-VALUE CONFUSION (FFPI). The ffpi note explicitly reasons 'p90 of 198 exceeds the March 2022 record, consistent with a ~40% chance of an all-time high by 2031.' That is invalid twice over: p90 of a terminal value is not the probability of a monthly series ever touching a barrier over 65 months, and with p50_2031 = 146 plus 12%/yr vol the running-max exceedance is 55-65%. The same error suppresses the 2036 figure below the point where the median path itself crosses 160.

DISCRETE RISK BELOW ITS OWN STATED BASE RATE (EPIZOOTIC). foodwater_livestock_epizootic_g20 states 6-7 events in 12 years across the G20 = 50-55%/yr, which implies 98% by 2031 under a Poisson process, yet reports 76%. Base rate cited, then not used.

HAZARD-RATE COLLAPSE WITHOUT MECHANISM (EXPORT BANS). foodwater_new_staple_export_bans is internally consistent with ~18%/yr onset for the 2027 cell (26%) but the 2031 (54%) and 2036 (68%) cells imply the hazard falls to 12%/yr then 8%/yr, with no stated reason and against a reinforcing feedback loop rated 0.75.

NEAR-EXCLUSIVE BRANCHES SUMMING PAST 100. P(urea monthly average >$800 by 2027) = 44 and P(Hormuz fertilizer flows normalise to 90% for three consecutive months by 2027) = 58 sum to 102. They are not strictly exclusive (a spike could precede normalisation) but they are close to it over a 17-month window, and the model does not acknowledge or price the overlap.

ANCHOR INCONSISTENCY (UREA). The indicator block lists benchmark urea at $435/t (28 July 2026); the urea_price continuous variable uses current_value 520 as a 'year-average anchor.' A forward-looking distribution should be anchored on the current spot, not on a backward-looking annual average that embeds the already-unwound March squeeze. This inflates the right tail (p90_2031 = 852) that in turn props up the >$800 discrete risk.

SUBSET/SUPERSET TIMING TENSION (FAMINES). foodwater_three_concurrent_famines is given 10% by 2027 while the May 2026 IPC finds ZERO areas currently in Famine. Reaching three concurrent confirmations requires at least three new confirmations with overlapping validity windows within 17 months — a strict and much rarer subset of the 68-74% 'at least one new famine' event, and 10% implies ~14% of new-famine worlds are triple-concurrent worlds within 17 months.

MISSING BLACK SEA UPSIDE BRANCH. The model includes a deliberate risk-off event for Hormuz (foodwater_hormuz_fertilizer_normalisation, 58/85/92) but none for the Black Sea, despite naming a Ukraine settlement as one of two 'fast geopolitical resolution' branches in structural uncertainties. This is an asymmetric treatment of two structurally identical shocks and biases the aggregate distribution toward grinding continuation.

missing_risks.name: Mississippi River or Panama Canal low-water event materially disrupts US grain exports
missing_risks.resolution_criteria: USDA Grain Transportation Report or Army Corps data show either (a) Mississippi barge freight rates above 800% of tariff benchmark, or draft/tow restrictions in force on the Lower Mississippi, for 30+ consecutive days, or (b) Panama Canal transit slots cut 30%+ below normal for 60+ consecutive days.
missing_risks.reasoning: A glaring omission for a domain that models Ukrainian and Hormuz logistics in detail. The Lower Mississippi carries roughly 60% of US grain exports and hit record-low water with barge restrictions in autumn 2022 AND autumn 2023 AND again in 2024 — three years in four. Panama Canal cut transits sharply in 2023-24. That is a recurrence rate near 60-75%/yr for at least one of the two, making a 5-year probability of 80% conservative. It is low-severity (rerouting and rail substitute, basis blows out rather than flat price) but it is precisely the kind of high-frequency logistics risk the model captures for Ukraine and ignores for the US. La Nina years following the 2026-27 El Nino are the canonical trigger window for autumn 2027-28.

missing_risks.name: New World screwworm or FMD establishes in the US or EU cattle herd
missing_risks.resolution_criteria: USDA APHIS, WOAH or the European Commission confirms sustained autochthonous transmission of New World screwworm (Cochliomyia hominivorax) north of the Mexico-US border, or an FMD outbreak in an FMD-free country of the G7, triggering a national movement standstill or export ban of 30+ days.
missing_risks.reasoning: The model's only animal-disease risk is a poultry/pig inventory metric, which misses the ruminant channel entirely. Screwworm re-emerged and moved steadily north through Central America and Mexico through 2024-25, with US border detections and APHIS emergency response; the 1950s-60s US infestation cost the cattle sector on the order of $1bn/yr in today's money. FMD in a G7 country (UK 2001, ~6m animals culled) is a live tail given global trade volumes and the 2025 German/Hungarian FMD detections that already triggered EU export suspensions. Beef is the highest-value protein complex and the one with the slowest herd-rebuild dynamics (4-6 years), so the price consequence outlasts the outbreak by far more than poultry.

missing_risks.name: Cyberattack or physical sabotage halts a top-5 global agri-food processor or a major water utility
missing_risks.resolution_criteria: A publicly confirmed cyber or sabotage incident forces a 7+ day shutdown of national-scale operations at a top-5 global meat, grain-trading or fertilizer company, or causes a 7+ day loss of service at a water utility serving 1m+ people, per company disclosure, CISA/ENISA advisory or national regulator.
missing_risks.reasoning: Wholly absent from a model that otherwise enumerates transmission channels carefully. JBS (2021, global beef plants halted, $11m ransom), Dole (2023), Sysco (2023), and repeated Iranian/Russian-attributed probes of US and Israeli water SCADA (Aliquippa PA 2023, Unitronics PLCs) establish a base rate of roughly one qualifying agri-food incident every 2-3 years, rising with state-actor involvement during the active Iran and Ukraine conflicts the model already assumes continue. The ABCD grain traders and four fertilizer majors are concentration points with the same single-point-of-failure geometry the model correctly identifies for layer flocks.

missing_risks.name: FAO declares a desert locust upsurge or plague affecting three or more countries
missing_risks.resolution_criteria: FAO Desert Locust Watch raises the situation to 'Upsurge' or 'Plague' with swarms reported in three or more countries simultaneously for 60+ days.
missing_risks.reasoning: Omitted despite being the classic ENSO-teleconnected agricultural shock and despite the model building its whole 2027 story on a strong El Nino. Major upsurges: 1986-89, 2003-05, 2020-22 — roughly 3 in 40 years (~7.5%/yr, ~33% per 5 years), but conditioned on Indian Ocean Dipole and cyclone-driven Empty Quarter rainfall, which strong El Nino years elevate. The 2020 upsurge hit 23 countries and cost an estimated $8.5bn in the Horn alone. It is also the risk most exposed to the funding collapse the model emphasises elsewhere: FAO locust surveillance and early control in Yemen and Somalia are donor-funded and were the first thing cut.

missing_risks.name: DAP/phosphate rock price exceeds US$1,000/tonne on a monthly average
missing_risks.resolution_criteria: World Bank Pink Sheet monthly average DAP (f.o.b. US Gulf) exceeds US$1,000 per tonne in any month.
missing_risks.reasoning: The model tracks nitrogen obsessively (three urea indicators, a dedicated urea risk and continuous variable) and mentions DAP only in passing as 'up sharply on doubled sulfur.' Phosphate is structurally the tighter market: Morocco/OCP plus China control the majority of traded volume, China has maintained phosphate export restrictions since 2021, and DAP already exceeded $950/t in 2022 and traded above $700 through 2025. Sulfur — 50% of traded volume removed by the same Hormuz event the model verifies — is the direct input to phosphoric acid, so the current shock hits phosphate harder than nitrogen, yet nitrogen gets the risk entry. Phosphorus also has no synthetic substitute, unlike nitrogen, so the demand response is a straight yield loss.

calibration.overall_bias: "Mixed, not uniformly dramatic — but the errors are systematic in a specific pattern: ACUTE, NARRATIVE-SALIENT SHOCKS are over-forecast while RECURRING, BORING, HIGH-FREQUENCY events and NOMINAL-THRESHOLD events are under-forecast. Over-forecast cluster (all tied to the three live July 2026 shocks the analyst just finished researching — textbook availability): urea >$800 (44 -> 25), global cereal -4% (31/47 -> 18/31), GRFC >300m near-term (38 -> 15), three concurrent famines (10/25/34 -> 5/16/25), Indus curtailment (9/24 -> 5/16), Colorado no-deal (45 -> 32). Suggested shrink factor on this cluster: 0.65. Under-forecast cluster (things that happen every year or two, or that inflation delivers for free): G20 epizootic (76 -> 90, below the analyst's OWN cited base rate), FFPI >160 (42/60 -> 58/82, a nominal barrier a 2.8%/yr drift walks through), export bans on the long horizon (68 -> 78), rice >$650 by 2036 (40 -> 50), GRFC >300m by 2031-36 (64/74 -> 72/86). Suggested inflation factor on this cluster: 1.25. Net global shrink factor: 0.90 — the domain is only mildly over-dramatic in aggregate, but that near-neutral average masks two offsetting biases of roughly 30% each in opposite directions, which is worse than a uniform bias because it distorts the relative ranking of risks. The single most consequential structural defect is that six discrete risks are quantified inconsistently with the continuous variables in the same document; the discrete probabilities appear to have been set by narrative feel and the continuous variables by statistical reasoning, and they were never reconciled. A mechanical fix — derive every threshold-crossing discrete probability from the corresponding continuous variable's RUNNING-MAXIMUM (or minimum) distribution rather than its terminal value — would resolve most of the coherence violations at once. Verdict is major_issues chiefly on the Colorado fixed-date structural error plus the six discrete/continuous contradictions, not on the quality of the underlying research, which is unusually good."

conditional_edges.mechanism: A blockade is the escalation rung below invasion: it mobilizes forces, burns the surprise option, and creates a use-it-or-lose-it dynamic if coercion fails to produce political capitulation.

Enforcing a quarantine requires interdicting shipping the US Navy is likely escorting or shadowing; close-quarters intercepts around a contested exclusion zone are the most likely path to a first fatality.
US forces are forward-deployed in the first island chain; an assault puts American ISR, submarine and air assets in direct contact almost immediately regardless of formal intervention decisions.

Yonaguni and the Senkakus sit inside the operational area, and US basing on Okinawa makes Japanese territory a belligerent staging ground with SDF units drawn into escort, minesweeping and air defense.
Roughly 90% of leading-edge logic and most advanced packaging transits Taiwan; even a non-kinetic quarantine forces a global repricing of technology earnings and of the equity risk premium.

Loss of Taiwanese foundry output plus sanctions on the largest manufacturing economy is a simultaneous supply shock to autos, electronics and capital goods, with contagion through trade credit and shipping insurance.
Coercion against Taiwan triggers immediate US and allied economic retaliation; average effective tariff rates jump as decoupling shifts from managed to punitive.
Rare earths and magnets are Beijing's principal non-military retaliation lever; a Taiwan crisis converts the standing export-control regime into an actual embargo on the US and EU.
Sanctions, capital flight, withdrawal of shipping insurance and collapse of export orders hit an economy already carrying a property and LGFV overhang.
Frontier training scale-up depends on TSMC N3/N2 wafer starts and CoWoS packaging; losing that supply caps accelerator production for years and delays the largest runs.
Open conflict makes licensing flagship datacenter GPUs to China politically impossible; the policy space collapses to full embargo.
Roughly a fifth of global liquids transits Hormuz and non-Gulf spare capacity cannot replace it; a sustained halving of transit is the canonical $120+ Brent trigger.
Once interdiction capability is demonstrated and the escalation taboo broken, repeat closures become a standing coercive tool rather than a one-off.
Qatari, Saudi and Iranian urea and ammonia plus their gas feedstock are chokepoint-dependent; loss of that tonnage alongside higher gas prices pushes urea above $800.
Near-definitional overlap: a settle above $120 during a sustained episode almost always drags the monthly average above the same threshold.
Energy passes directly into headline CPI and indirectly into goods and transport services within two to three quarters.
A doubling of crude acts as a tax on oil-importing consumers while forcing central banks to hold rates high into weakening demand.
Fuel, freight and nitrogen fertilizer are the dominant non-land cost lines in grain production; crude spikes propagate into the FAO index with a two- to three-quarter lag.
Iran crossing the threshold is itself an instance of the target event, and additionally raises Saudi and Turkish hedging.
Near-identical event definitions; these should be treated as one underlying state transition observed by two indicators.
A durable ceasefire removes the active front where NATO-Russia incidents originate and signals Russian acceptance of a frozen line.
Odesa corridor throughput depends almost entirely on the absence of strikes on port infrastructure and on war-risk insurance rates.
Ceasefire strips the war-risk premium out of European gas and reopens the possibility of partial transit resumption.
Arms control historically requires a baseline of non-belligerency; a ceasefire restores the diplomatic channel needed for a deployed-warhead cap.
A successor lacks personal ownership of the war and typically needs to consolidate domestically, making a settlement politically cheaper.
Loss of the US extended-deterrence guarantee is the strongest documented driver of indigenous proliferation decisions in Poland, South Korea and Japan.
Overlapping definitions of the same class of event, differing mainly in attribution requirement and outage threshold.
Allied doctrine since 2021 explicitly contemplates cyber operations meeting the armed-attack threshold; a state-attributed multi-day blackout is the canonical test case.
Direct NATO-Russia conventional war is the highest-probability pathway to first nuclear use, via Russian escalate-to-de-escalate doctrine under conventional disadvantage.
Short warning times, Pakistani first-use doctrine under conventional inferiority, and the absence of a reliable crisis-communication channel make this the second most likely nuclear pathway.
Pakistan has repeatedly declared physical interference with western-river flows an act of war; roughly 80% of its irrigated agriculture depends on them.
Water is India's principal sub-kinetic escalation lever and has been threatened in every recent crisis.
An aggregate 20% decline in hyperscaler capex is essentially impossible without at least one top-4 firm guiding down; the indicators nest.
Hyperscaler capex is the dominant revenue line for accelerator demand; a guide-down invalidates the growth narrative supporting the multiple.
Extreme index concentration means the AI complex now dominates S&P drawdown risk; a halving of the largest constituent mechanically drags the index.
Datacenter construction and equipment have become a material share of US private fixed investment growth; its reversal removes the main non-consumption growth impulse.
Frontier training is funded by continuous external capital; a funding-window closure forces the marginal lab to exit, merge, or retreat to applications.
Datacenter interconnection queues are a leading driver of tight-reserve-margin risk in PJM and ERCOT; capex retrenchment relieves near-term load growth.
Task-horizon length has tracked effective compute closely; an order-of-magnitude larger run is the main mechanism by which the horizon extends.
Month-long autonomous task reliability is the threshold at which agents substitute for whole job functions rather than tasks, making explicit AI attribution of large cuts defensible to boards.
Attribution cascades are self-reinforcing across peer firms; concentrated white-collar displacement raises aggregate unemployment when the hiring rate is already low.
Long-horizon autonomy is precisely the capability that converts model-assisted intrusion into end-to-end autonomous campaigns at scale.
A salient AI-caused catastrophe shifts Congress toward regulation and makes broad preemption of state safety laws politically toxic.
An acknowledged uplift incident demonstrates the capability pathway is reachable, indicating the barrier between design assistance and lethal deployment has thinned.
Definitionally nested: an AI-assisted biological attack with 10+ deaths is a deliberate biological attack with 10+ deaths.
Domestic EUV destroys the leverage rationale for controls; the policy argument shifts to capturing revenue before the market is lost permanently.
Visible load shedding converts diffuse ratepayer resentment about datacenter-driven bills into statutory action by state legislatures.
US demand plus dollar funding conditions dominate the world growth aggregate; sub-2% world growth rarely occurs without a US contraction.
Commodity revenue collapse plus dollar strength plus closed primary markets is the standard EM sovereign distress transmission chain.
Demand destruction against sticky OPEC+ and shale supply produces sharp price undershoots.
Valuation marks lag public markets; redemption demand concentrates on semi-liquid vehicles precisely when exits and refinancing close.
Bank lending to private credit and NDFI exposures has grown to systemic scale; gating reveals mark inadequacy and triggers funding withdrawal from the most levered intermediaries.
Credit intermediation shocks transmit to investment and hiring faster than any other financial channel.
A second inflation peak destroys the disinflation term-premium narrative and forces repricing of both the policy path and the inflation risk premium.
Japanese institutions are the largest foreign holders of Treasuries; domestic yields above hedged foreign returns trigger repatriation and steepen the global long end.
Global duration shocks hit the most fiscally exposed sovereigns first; French and Italian debt trajectories have no room for a higher risk-free anchor.
The sovereign-bank doom loop remains intact: domestic banks hold the sovereign paper whose spread widens.
Growth materially below target is the historical trigger for central-government balance-sheet deployment on property and LGFV debt.
China is roughly half of refined copper demand; a growth shortfall removes the marginal buyer that a $15,000 print requires.
The licensing architecture is the precondition for a targeted cutoff; once in force, denial becomes an administrative decision rather than a new policy.
A magnet embargo halting Western auto and defense production forces immediate tariff retaliation.
Invocation over a state's objection places federalized forces and state-controlled National Guard under competing command authorities in the same physical space.
Once judicial arbitration is removed, states have no non-physical remedy against federal action they deem unlawful.
V-Dem's electoral-autocracy coding weights judicial constraints on the executive heavily; open defiance is close to a scoring trigger on its own.
A third-term bid is unambiguously barred by the 22nd Amendment, so pursuing it presupposes willingness to override adverse judicial rulings.
Fiscal-expansion commitments plus confrontation with the EU framework from the euro area's second-largest economy widen OAT-Bund directly.
ENSO explains most interannual global-mean temperature variance; a very strong event delivers its peak warming to the following calendar year.
Very strong El Nino produces the basin-scale thermal stress patterns that drove the 1998, 2016 and 2023-24 global bleaching events.
Strong El Nino is the main known driver of spatially correlated breadbasket failure, hitting Australian wheat, Southeast Asian rice and Southern African maize simultaneously.
Repeated single years well above 1.6C are the empirical basis on which assessment bodies declare the multi-decadal mean breached.
Sustained wet-bulb 35C exceeds unassisted human thermoregulation; in a densely populated, grid-fragile region it produces mass mortality directly.
Governance regimes for novel technologies are almost always reactive; unilateral deployment forces the negotiation that voluntary processes have not produced.
Observed 30% weakening is the primary empirical evidence any tipping declaration would rest on.
Stocks absorb the production shortfall first; a 4% global drop draws the buffer down within one marketing year.
Grain price convexity to low stocks-to-use is the best-established relationship in agricultural economics.
Thin buffers plus rising domestic prices produce the beggar-thy-neighbour export-restriction cascade seen in 2008, 2010 and 2022.
Rice is the thinnest major staple market; Indian or Vietnamese restrictions move the Thai benchmark within weeks.
Same underlying index and threshold observed by two separate nodes.
Import-dependent low-income countries convert world price shocks into acute food insecurity within two quarters, amplified by currency depreciation.
Urban staple price spikes are the most reliable precursor of mass protest in low-income urbanizing states.
The tail of the acute-insecurity distribution scales with its mass; more people in IPC3+ mechanically raises the count of populations tipping into IPC5.
Famine declarations in recent decades have been prevented mainly by external ration delivery; funding collapse removes the suppressing intervention.
The Indo-Gangetic plain produces roughly a seventh of global wheat; a virulent rust or blast epidemic there is one of few single-region events large enough to move the world aggregate.
Sustained human-to-human transmission of a novel subtype is the operative criterion for WHO pandemic declaration.
Every declared influenza pandemic of the modern era except 2009 exceeded a million deaths; H5 case fatality would make the threshold near-certain.
Behavioural withdrawal and policy restrictions produce simultaneous supply and demand contraction across all major economies.
Large poultry and swine epizootics expand the mammalian and human exposure surface where reassortment and adaptive mutation occur.
Federal de-recommendation removes insurance coverage mandates and school-entry justification, dropping MMR coverage below the herd-immunity threshold in additional counties.
Civil war in a 50-million-plus country is the dominant single source of new large-scale forced displacement.

latent_factors.name: Great-power hostility and bloc hardening
latent_factors.description: Unobserved intensity of confrontation between the US-led bloc and the China/Russia/Iran/DPRK alignment. Drives simultaneous escalation across theatres, weaponization of trade and technology chokepoints, arms-control failure, and proliferation hedging, even where no direct causal link exists between specific incidents.

latent_factors.name: Global fiscal and financial fragility
latent_factors.description: Latent thinness of balance-sheet buffers: sovereign debt trajectories, term premia, leverage in non-bank intermediation, and stretched risk-asset valuations. Raises the probability that any given shock propagates into funding stress rather than being absorbed.

latent_factors.name: Climate forcing and hydrological stress intensity
latent_factors.description: Realized strength of the physical climate signal over the window: ocean heat content, ENSO amplitude, land-carbon feedback and continental drought severity. Correlates temperature records, ecosystem thresholds, extreme heat mortality and agricultural shortfalls without any of them causing the others.

latent_factors.name: Institutional legitimacy erosion and state capacity decay
latent_factors.description: Unobserved decline in the ability of governments and international bodies to command compliance, deliver public goods and constrain executives. Correlates democratic backsliding, coups, political violence, public-health governance failure and multilateral paralysis across otherwise unrelated countries and domains.

latent_factors.name: AI capability and compute-investment intensity
latent_factors.description: Latent rate of frontier capability progress and the capital cycle financing it. High values pull capability, energy-demand, labour-displacement and misuse nodes together; the factor's collapse phase pulls the capex, valuation and lab-failure nodes together instead, hence their negative loadings.

latent_factors.name: Biological and health-system fragility
latent_factors.description: Unobserved combination of pathogen emergence pressure, surveillance quality, vaccine confidence and outbreak-response funding. Correlates zoonotic emergence, epidemic escalation, vaccine-preventable disease resurgence and AMR independently of any single outbreak's causal chain.

blocking_pairs.reason: Brent monthly averages above $120 and below $45 sit at opposite ends of the same price distribution; both occurring in one window requires an extreme boom-bust sequence, so they should be strongly negatively coupled within any period.
Same underlying oil price state observed at opposite thresholds; a sustained supply-shock regime and a demand-collapse regime substitute for each other.
A durable 180-day Russia-Ukraine ceasefire and an Article 5 invocation against a Russian attack describe incompatible states of the Russia-West relationship in the same period.
A binding US-China frontier-compute agreement requires a functioning bilateral negotiating relationship that an invasion of Taiwan eliminates entirely.

Licensing flagship datacenter GPUs for general commercial sale to China is politically unavailable once US and PRC forces have exchanged lethal fire; the two policies belong to opposite strategic postures.
Regime collapse removes the institutional actor pursuing weaponization; a successful test and the end of the governing system are strongly substitutive paths for the Iranian nuclear file.
Sustained effective closure of the strait and normalisation of Gulf fertilizer flows through that same strait are directly contradictory states.
The oil-demand-peak node is explicitly defined as a year-on-year decline occurring outside recession or supply shock, so a global recession year disqualifies the observation by construction.
Rejoining WHO and federally de-recommending a core childhood vaccine represent opposite directions of the same US public-health governance posture and are unlikely to coexist.
US withdrawal and a functioning collective-defence invocation reflect incompatible states of alliance credibility; the withdrawal path substitutes for the collective-response path.

Substitutive policy worlds: confirmed emissions peaking reduces the desperation premium behind unilateral solar radiation management, while unilateral deployment typically presupposes mitigation failure.

Weak substitution rather than strict exclusion: the political configuration that cuts a G7 country's permanent immigration by three quarters correlates with the public-health disinvestment that keeps US life expectancy short of 80 years.

coupling.notes:
Roughly 120 candidate edges were drafted and trimmed to 89 with defensible transmission channels. Things the sampler author needs to know:

(1) DEFINITIONAL NEAR-DUPLICATES. Several catalog pairs measure the same underlying state: economy_oil_120 / energy_oil_price_spike_120; climate_food_price_shock / foodwater_ffpi_above_160 (both FAO index >160); geopolitics_grid_cyberattack_nato / energy_grid_cyber_major_outage; geopolitics_iran_regime_change / politics_iran_islamic_republic_ends; geopolitics_hormuz_major_closure / economy_hormuz_closure / energy_hormuz_reclosure; ai_bio_mass_casualty / health_bioterror_attack_10_deaths; demographics_china_census_downward_revision / demographics_china_population_below_1_4bn; health_us_measles_5000_cases / health_us_measles_elimination_revoked. I encoded these as very high multipliers (15-25) at ~zero lag rather than merging nodes. Note their marginals are mutually inconsistent (Hormuz at 70/34/22%, measles at 42/88%), which signals the definitions differ more than the labels suggest — either reconcile them or force near-deterministic linkage, otherwise the sim will produce incoherent joint counts.

(2) WHERE THE MASS CONCENTRATES. Four hubs carry most of the correlated tail: (a) Taiwan blockade at 14% is the pivot node — it propagates into equities, global recession, tariffs, rare earths, Chinese growth and Japan while simultaneously suppressing AI scaling and export-control relaxation; (b) Hormuz at a 70% marginal is the single highest-leverage aggravating source in the whole model, feeding oil, CPI, rates, fertilizer and food; (c) the AI capex chain (capex bust -> guide-down -> Nvidia -> S&P -> private credit -> banks -> global recession) is fully connected and will generate most correlated financial-crisis mass; (d) the food chain (El Nino -> cereal drop -> stocks-to-use -> FAO index -> export bans -> rice, then out into African unrest). Expect a fat compound-shock mode around 2027-28 combining El Nino-driven multi-breadbasket failure, a Hormuz episode, and food-price-driven political instability.

(3) PROTECTIVE EDGES ARE SPARSE BUT LOAD-BEARING. geopolitics_ukraine_durable_ceasefire (78% marginal) is the main risk-off hub; without its four protective edges the model badly overstates European tail risk. economy_ai_capex_bust -> energy_us_firm_load_shed (0.55) and economy_china_sub4_growth -> energy_copper_price_shock (0.5) are the main channels by which one bad outcome reduces another.

(4) LAG CONVENTIONS. Lags are years from source firing to the target's hazard multiplier taking effect. Financial contagion 0.1-0.4y; macro transmission 0.3-0.7y; political/electoral 0.5-1.5y; structural/climatic 0.7-1.5y. Zero-lag edges encode definitional nesting, not causation.

(5) AVOID DOUBLE-COUNTING LATENTS AND EDGES. Several pairs are connected both by an explicit edge and by a shared latent (the Taiwan nodes, the financial cluster, the food-climate cluster). Applying both at full strength will materially overstate tail joint probabilities. Recommend either shrinking loadings ~30% where an explicit edge already exists, or applying latents only to baseline hazard before edge multipliers.

(6) NEGATIVE LOADINGS ENCODE THE GOOD-WORLD DIRECTION. Arms-control deals, a US-China AI agreement, WHO re-entry, pandemic agreement entry into force, methane growth halting, polio interruption and confirmed CO2 peaking all load negatively and should co-occur in benign draws. Without them the simulation is uniformly doom-weighted, which is itself a modelling error.

(7) DELIBERATE OMISSIONS. Demographic nodes (China/Japan births, India census, China population) are near-deterministic at these marginals and essentially exogenous to everything else here — treat them as slow-moving context, not cascade participants. Same for energy_solar_terawatt_year and energy_hydrogen_scale_milestone. I also declined to wire climate_heat_event_100k_deaths -> climate_srm_unilateral_deployment and several NATO-withdrawal -> EU-politics edges: plausible stories, but the evidence base does not support a specific multiplier.

redteam.lens: Structural-break / inside-view: where the 1950-2025 generating process is dead and the model is still sampling from it
redteam.headline_critique:
This parameter set has one systematic, diagnosable failure, and it is not "too dramatic." It is that **threshold events on already-trending variables are priced as surprises rather than as trend arrivals.** Wherever a discrete risk sits on top of a continuous generator in `params/world_model.json`, the discrete node sits below what the model's own drift and quantiles imply — 12 of 12 cases I checked, all in the same direction. That is a bias, not noise.

The clearest instance: `frontier_train_flop_log10` has `p10_2031 = 28.0`, sitting exactly on the 1e28 threshold. The model's own generator therefore says ~93% by 2031. The discrete node says 58%. Same pattern on `metr_horizon_log2_hours` (generator 63% terminal, node 55%, and the node is a ratchet so it should exceed terminal), `global_tfr` (39% terminal, node 20%), `china_gdp_growth` (71% for the 2031 print alone, node 52% cumulative — a cumulative below a single in-window year is a hard incoherence).

The mechanism is double-discounting. The analyst bends the trend once when setting the continuous drift (METR: naive drift 1.3 gives 8.62 by 2031, they wrote 8.1), then applies the same "exponentials bend, base rates rule" haircut again at the discrete node. The reference class is invoked twice against evidence it has already been charged for.

Where the regime is genuinely broken, this bites hardest. Fertility: the UN transition model assumes convergence to ~1.8 and a floor. Observed global TFR fell 2.72→2.25 in nine years (−0.05/yr) against the model's assumed −0.022/yr, and every WPP/IHME revision since 2015 has moved down — serially correlated revisions are the signature of a prior the data keeps breaking. China growth: "Beijing prints within 0.3pp of target" was generated by land finance and property, which have ended; the target now follows the economy, and the model's own −0.24pp/yr drift concedes it.

Conversely, the pure-shock geopolitical nodes (Article 5, Taiwan invasion, nuclear use, grid cyber) are defensible or mildly high. The catalog is well-calibrated on things that go bang and badly complacent on things that arrive on schedule.

specific_corrections.claim: 58% by 2031 that a single training run of >=1e28 FLOP is publicly reported
specific_corrections.evidence: Largest generator contradiction in the set. The model's own continuous node frontier_train_flop_log10 has current_value 26.7, annual_drift 0.42, and p10_2031 = 28.0 — the 10th percentile world in 2031 sits EXACTLY on the 1e28 threshold. Terminal-2031 exceedance under the stated p50=28.8/p90=29.5 (implied sd 0.55) is 92.8%. Central crossing is (28.0-26.7)/0.42 = 3.1 years, i.e. late 2029. This is also a ratchet event, so path probability >= terminal probability. Corroborating own nodes: hyperscaler_capex_usd_b p50_2031=980bn, global_dc_electricity_twh p50_2031=1030. The only legitimate haircut is the 'publicly reported' clause, since labs stopped disclosing compute post-2023 — but Epoch-style capex/GPU-hour reconstruction is routinely treated as public reporting. An ~8pp disclosure discount off 93% gives 85%. 58% is the pre-2023 disclosure regime being applied to a post-2023 world.

specific_corrections.claim: 20% by 2031 that best-available global TFR falls below 2.1
specific_corrections.evidence: Double structural break, and the model's own generator already contradicts the node. global_tfr: current 2.23, p50_2031 = 2.12, p10_2031 = 2.03, giving implied sd 0.070 and terminal P(<2.10) = 38.8%. Because drift is downward, the path minimum is below terminal, so first-passage is ~43-46%. The node says 20% — under by a factor of 2.2 against the analyst's own numbers. Separately, the assumed drift of -0.022/yr is itself a dead-regime parameter: observed global TFR fell 2.72 (2015) to ~2.25 (2024), i.e. -0.05/yr, more than double. At -0.04/yr the threshold is crossed around 2029, inside the window. The UN demographic-transition prior assumes convergence to ~1.8 with a floor; the actual middle-income data (Thailand 0.95, Chile 1.03, Colombia 1.06, China ~1.0) show no floor and were predicted by no pre-2015 model. Serially-correlated downward WPP/IHME revisions since 2015 are the diagnostic that the prior, not the data, is wrong.

specific_corrections.claim: 52% by 2031 that China reports annual real GDP growth below 4.0%
specific_corrections.evidence: Hard incoherence: a cumulative any-year probability cannot sit below the probability of a single year inside the window. china_gdp_growth has p50_2031 = 3.4 and p90_2031 = 4.8 (implied sd 1.09), so P(the 2031 print alone is below 4.0) = 70.9%. I simulated the any-year-through-2031 event on the model's own declining mean path (4.36, 4.12, 3.88, 3.64, 3.40) with a common-factor correlation structure: 79% at rho=0.8, 86% at rho=0.6, 98% independent. Even at implausibly high persistence the answer is ~79%, not 52%. The base rate being defended ('two sub-4 prints in 35 years; Beijing hits target') was generated by land finance, property and export-led investment, all of which the model's own -0.24pp/yr drift concedes have ended. Beijing has already published 2.2% (2020) and 3.0% (2022), and the target now follows the economy — once the announced target is 'around 4%', a 3.8% print is politically routine.

specific_corrections.claim: 55% by 2031 that a frontier agent reaches a 167-hour 50%-reliability horizon
specific_corrections.evidence: Double-discounting, verifiable against the model's own numbers. metr_horizon_log2_hours: current 1.6, drift 1.3, p50_2031 = 8.1, p90_2031 = 10.8. The threshold is log2(167) = 7.38, so terminal-2031 exceedance is 63.3% on the stated quantiles alone — and this is a ratchet (published horizons do not regress), so the by-2031 probability must EXCEED terminal exceedance, putting it at 68-72%. The analyst already bent the trend once inside the generator: naive drift 1.3 over 5.4 years gives 8.62, but they wrote p50 = 8.1, an explicit deceleration haircut. Applying the 'exponentials saturate in 5-8 years' reference class again at the discrete node charges the same evidence twice. Note also their own p10_2031 = 5.4 log2 = 42 hours, meaning the stall scenario is already priced at 10%. The one legitimate residual is METR ceasing to be able to run the eval at that length, which is a resolution-infrastructure risk worth a few points, not 13.

specific_corrections.claim: 34% by 2031 that US total fertility rate falls below 1.50
specific_corrections.evidence: us_total_fertility_rate: current 1.585, drift -0.012, p50_2031 = 1.51, p10_2031 = 1.44, implied sd 0.055. Terminal P(<1.50) = 42.7%, and with downward drift the path minimum makes first-passage ~48-52%. The node says 34%. Beyond the arithmetic, there is a specific mechanical channel the model has in its own parameters but does not connect: us_net_international_migration has p10_2031 = -150 (negative net migration). A negative-NIM regime shrinks the 20-34 female population that forms the denominator of age-specific rates, while Hispanic-origin TFR has already converged toward non-Hispanic white levels far faster than any Census projection assumed. US TFR has fallen in every year since 2007 except 2014 and the 2021 blip; the mean-reverting post-recession-recovery prior that supports 34% belongs to the 1976-2007 regime.

specific_corrections.claim: 83% by 2031 that a calendar year reaches 1.65C above pre-industrial
specific_corrections.evidence: Computed directly from the analyst's own stated distributions. Their 2027 central is 1.68C with sd 0.09 (P = 63% for that year alone); subsequent years follow the model's gmst_anomaly_era5 drift of 0.025/yr from 1.47 with sd 0.10. Multiplying the miss probabilities across 2027-2031 gives P(no year >= 1.65) = 6.6%, i.e. 93.4%. The model's own gmst p50_2031 = 1.62 with p90_2031 = 1.78 independently makes 1.65 an ordinary rather than extreme outcome by the end of the window. Structurally, the 0.025C/yr drift is itself the 1970-2020 trend applied to a post-2020 forcing regime: the 2015-2024 decadal rate ran ~0.31C/decade against the assumed 0.25, because IMO 2020 shipping-sulphur cuts and Chinese SO2 controls unmasked forcing the historical trend had suppressed. The committed-forcing break argues the generator is also under-drifted, but 92% follows from the analyst's numbers as written without needing that.

specific_corrections.claim: 21% by 2031 that a new state tests or is confirmed to possess a nuclear weapon
specific_corrections.evidence: The 1970-2025 nonproliferation record was generated by three things that are simultaneously broken in this model's own world: a credible US extended deterrent (geo_us_milex_pct_gdp drift +0.02 while geo_europe_nato_milex_pct_gdp drifts +0.13 — the model itself encodes burden-shifting), a functioning NPT/IAEA monitoring regime (Iranian monitoring collapsed, NPT-withdrawal legislation live), and bilateral cap norms (New START expired Feb 2026; geo_deployed_strategic_warheads drift +95/yr with p50_2031 = 3720, the first sustained increase since 1986). Add the demonstration effect: a non-nuclear NPT signatory was decapitated by air campaign. Libya 2003 took eight years to teach the same lesson; this one is immediate. The brake is real and is why I move only 7 points — weaponisation has multi-year observable lead time and the criterion requires a test, declaration or public IAEA/USIC assessment. The larger error is the 2036 figure of 36%, which implies ~0.045/yr, only 1.25x the 1998-2026 rate, in a world where every restraint has been removed; 2036 should be ~46%.

specific_corrections.claim: 42% by 2031 that global oil demand declines year-on-year outside recession or supply shock
specific_corrections.evidence: Internal contradiction where the CONTINUOUS node is the dead-regime one. global_oil_demand_mbd carries drift +0.35/yr with p50_2031 = 106.3, a straight-line extrapolation. But the same parameter file has global_ev_share_pct going 22.4 to p50_2031 = 40 (drift +3.5/yr), global_solar_additions_gw p50_2031 = 880, and battery_pack_price_usd_kwh falling to 72. A 40% EV sales share compounding into the fleet subtracts roughly 1.5-2.5 mb/d of gasoline demand by 2031 relative to trend; that is not compatible with +0.35 mb/d/yr growth. The S-curve adoption regime has no analogue in the 1965-2020 oil-demand reference class the +0.35 drift is drawn from, and China — the entire source of marginal demand growth in that reference class — is now the fastest EV adopter. Either the continuous or the discrete node must move; the continuous one is anchored on the dead regime. The same critique applies to fossil_co2_emissions (drift +0.05, p50_2031 = 38.3, above the record) versus climate_fossil_co2_confirmed_peak at 52%.

specific_corrections.claim: 92% by 2031 that China annual births fall below 7.0 million
specific_corrections.evidence: Slow-moving certainty under-rated — the mild version of the same bias. china_annual_births: current 7.92, drift -0.34/yr, p50_2031 = 5.9, p90_2031 = 7.4. The MEDIAN 2031 world is 2.0 million births below the threshold, and even the 90th-percentile world (7.4) is only one year of drift above it. Central crossing is (7.92-7.0)/0.34 = 2.7 years, i.e. 2029, with four subsequent years of draws. Resolving NO requires births to flatten essentially immediately and stay flat, against a cohort effect already locked in: the number of women aged 20-34 falls ~20% over the window regardless of any TFR recovery, and the model's own china_share_60_plus drift of +0.85/yr encodes that age structure. The 8pp of residual probability at 92% is doing no work the age pyramid has not already removed.

specific_corrections.claim: 5% by 2031 for US initiating Article 13 withdrawal, used as the alliance-commitment node
specific_corrections.evidence: The number is fine; the node is measuring a dead variable. Article 13 is a treaty-membership formality never invoked in 77 years and requiring Senate consent or an act of Congress under the FY2024 NDAA. Meanwhile the actual structural break — the credibility of the guarantee — is happening entirely in continuous space the discrete catalog does not read: geo_us_milex_pct_gdp flat at drift +0.02 while geo_europe_nato_milex_pct_gdp drifts +0.13, force reductions in Germany, an explicit posture review, and a guarantee publicly conditioned on spending. A US that has withdrawn its conventional forces and conditioned Article 5 is fully hollowed out at Article 13 = 0%. Every downstream node that should depend on alliance credibility — new_nuclear_weapons_state, nato_article5_invoked, china_taiwan_quarantine_or_blockade — is therefore reading a parent that cannot fire. The fix is a replacement node: 'US formally conditions or qualifies its Article 5 commitment in an official strategy document, or withdraws >50% of permanently stationed European ground forces', which I would put at ~35% by 2031.

redteam.systematic_bias_estimate:
TOO COMPLACENT, and specifically so — not uniformly. The bias is concentrated in one identifiable node class and is close to absent elsewhere.

Measured: across the 12 nodes where a discrete threshold risk sits on top of a continuous generator in the model's own parameter file, the discrete node understates the generator-implied probability in 12 of 12 cases. Mean gap is +16.1 percentage points; mean log-odds gap is 0.87, i.e. the affected nodes run at roughly 1/2.4 of the odds their own generators imply (median 1/1.9). Directional unanimity at n=12 has a null probability of 2^-12 = 0.024%, so this is a bias, not sampling noise.

Diagnosis: double-discounting. The analyst bends the trend once when eliciting the continuous drift (METR naive 8.62 written as 8.1; global TFR observed -0.05/yr written as -0.022), then applies the same base-rate/reference-class haircut again at the discrete threshold. The reference class is charged twice against evidence it has already been paid for. Because the engine calibrates baselines to reproduce the elicited discrete marginals (README: "coupling reshapes the joint distribution, not the marginals"), this bias survives calibration untouched — the simulation faithfully reproduces the understatement, and the continuous variables and the discrete risks can disagree by a factor of two without any test failing. That is a structural gap in the engine, not just in the parameters: there is no consistency check binding a threshold node to its own generator.

Scope: I would apply a +1.9x to +2.4x odds correction to roughly 25-35 of the 159 nodes — the trend-arrival class (AI compute and capability, fertility, China growth, committed climate forcing, JGB/UST/reserve-share duration nodes, EV and oil demand). Median correction for those: +12 to +25pp.

For the pure-shock class — Article 5, Taiwan invasion, nuclear use in anger, grid cyberattack, AMOC tipping, unilateral SRM, UNSC expansion — the parameters are defensible or mildly too dramatic, and I would not move them upward on structural-break grounds. Several (grid_cyberattack_nato 20%, wetbulb_35c 30%, arctic_practically_ice_free 4%) are too high against zero-instance records.

Net verdict: too complacent by roughly 1.5x in odds on the affected subset, approximately unbiased on the shock subset, therefore mildly too complacent overall. The catalog is well-calibrated on things that go bang and poorly calibrated on things that arrive on schedule — exactly backwards for a decade in which the arriving things are the ones whose generating processes have changed.
missing_scenarios: Nuclear uploading with no discrete node. The model forecasts geo_deployed_strategic_warheads rising +95/yr to a 2031 median of 3720, yet there is no risk for 'US or Russia publicly exceeds the former New START ceiling of 1,550 deployed strategic warheads.' That is the most legible, most likely-to-fire post-arms-control event in the window (~55% by 2031), and the natural parent for new_nuclear_weapons_state, us_russia_strategic_arms_deal and dprk_nuclear_test. Its absence means the proliferation cascade runs off Iran and ROK narratives rather than off the arms-race variable the model already tracks.

Taiwan semiconductor disruption decoupled from military action. The catalog prices invasion (6%) and quarantine (14%) but has no node for 'TSMC advanced-node (<=5nm) output falls >=50% for >=3 months for any cause.' The transmission channel that makes Taiwan matter to the economy and AI domains can fire without a shot: a Hualien-class earthquake, grid instability under AI load, a cyber incident, or an export-control action on Taiwan-fabbed Chinese-designed silicon. Conditioning the semiconductor shock exclusively on PLA action understates it substantially; I would put the disruption node at ~18% by 2031 against a ~20% union of the military nodes.

State capture or requisition of frontier compute. The catalog has ai_state_datacenter_moratorium (58%) and ai_export_controls_relaxed (42%) but nothing in the seizure direction: a US Defense Production Act invocation over datacenter capacity or GPU allocation, a sovereign taking an equity or golden-share position in a frontier lab, or a national-security review blocking a training run. With hyperscaler_capex_usd_b at a 2031 median of 980bn and frontier_lab_arr_usd_b at 350bn, compute becomes strategically indistinguishable from enrichment capacity, and the historical analogue (uranium, telecoms, 1980s semiconductors) is state intervention, not laissez-faire. ~30% by 2031.

Extended-deterrence intermediate step. Between the status quo and geopolitics_new_nuclear_weapons_state there is a far more likely observable that is absent: 'a US ally formally requests, or the US agrees to, forward-deployment of US nuclear weapons or a NATO-style nuclear-sharing arrangement in ROK, Poland, or Japan.' This is the step that either relieves or confirms proliferation pressure, has live political support in two of the three, and fires years before any indigenous programme would. ~30% by 2031. Without it the proliferation node has no early-warning parent and the cascade is all-or-nothing.

Upward revision of committed warming. Every climate node treats the forcing as known and asks only whether thresholds are crossed. There is no node for 'IPCC AR7, WMO, or an equivalent assessment formally revises equilibrium climate sensitivity, the aerosol-masking term, or the remaining 1.5C carbon budget materially upward.' The 2023-2024 anomaly the analyst repeatedly calls partly unexplained is precisely the observation that would force such a revision, and AR7 lands inside the window. This is the climate analogue of a parameter-world shift and would move a dozen downstream nodes at once. ~35% by 2031.

Demographic repricing event. The catalog covers births and TFR thresholds but not the institutional consequence that makes them matter: 'UN WPP or a G7 sovereign officially revises its long-run population or dependency-ratio projection down enough to trigger a pension or sovereign-debt reassessment (a rating action, or a statutory retirement-age change of >=2 years in a G7 country).' Fertility collapse transmits to the economy domain through fiscal projections, not birth counts, and no node currently carries that edge. ~40% by 2031.

Collapse of the AI evaluation and disclosure regime. Several AI nodes (ai_metr_month_horizon, ai_1e28_flop_run, ai_china_leaderboard_top) depend on third parties continuing to measure and publish. There is no node for 'frontier labs collectively cease providing pre-deployment access to independent evaluators, or compute ceases to be reconstructable from public data.' This is a resolution-infrastructure risk that would render multiple nodes permanently NO regardless of underlying capability — a systematic downward bias on the whole AI block currently smuggled into the capability estimates rather than modelled explicitly. ~25% by 2031.

redteam.lens: Outside-view / base-rate hazard audit: implied per-year hazards recomputed from each p2031 and compared against the model's own stated reference classes and the 75-year historical record
redteam.headline_critique:
Converting every p2031 to a per-year hazard (window = 5.42 years, h = -ln(1-p)/5.42) and comparing it to the base_rate_anchor the model itself wrote produces one clean, quantified finding: **the catalog discounts what it has counted and inflates what it has not.**

For nodes whose reference class contains zero or one historical instance, the implied hazard runs 2-8x the model's own stated base rate. politics_us_open_defiance_supreme_court: anchor "under 0.5%/yr", implied 4.1%/yr (8.2x). politics_us_armed_federal_state_confrontation: anchor "well under 0.5%/yr", implied 2.6%/yr — above even the rule-of-three 95% upper bound (3/150 = 2.0%/yr) for 150 years of zeros. geopolitics_grid_cyberattack_nato: anchor "well under 1%/yr", implied 4.1%/yr, for an event two-to-three orders of magnitude beyond anything ever achieved (Ukraine 2015: 230k customers, 6 hours). climate_wetbulb_35c_sustained implies 6.6%/yr for a three-hour exceedance with zero confirmed instances in 45 years.

For nodes whose reference class is well populated, the implied hazard runs 0.5-0.75x the stated base rate. foodwater_livestock_epizootic_g20: anchor 50-55%/yr, implied 26%/yr — the model halved its own number. economy_large_bank_failure: anchor ~10%/yr, implied 5.5%/yr. health_pandemic_1m_deaths: anchor post-1970 3.6%/yr, implied 2.36%/yr, discounted for "improved countermeasures" that COVID already falsified. politics_us_federal_official_assassinated: anchor ~3%/yr, implied 2.35%/yr, in a scenario the model elsewhere describes as the most violent US political environment in decades. politics_xi_departure rests on a base-rate anchor that counts only Hua Guofeng, omitting Hu Yaobang (1987) and Zhao Ziyang (1989) — both sitting General Secretaries removed, which is exactly what the criterion asks — understating the political-removal hazard by roughly an order of magnitude.

Median ratio (implied hazard ÷ own anchor): ~3.5x for zero-instance classes, ~0.65x for populated classes. That ~5x divergence is the signature of narrative-driven rather than frequency-driven parameterization. Separately, the duplicate-family resolver picks geopolitics_hormuz_major_closure (70%) as representative over economy_hormuz_closure (22%) and energy_hormuz_reclosure (34%) — selecting the member with the *strictest* bar and the *highest* probability, a logical nesting inversion that propagates the most dramatic member into the simulation.

specific_corrections.claim: 20% by 2031 that the executive openly defies a final, non-stayed SCOTUS order for 30+ days
specific_corrections.evidence: Implied hazard 4.1%/yr against the model's OWN stated anchor of 'under 0.5%/yr' — an 8.2x uplift with no explicit evidence budget. Zero clean instances in 235 years (Jackson 1832: no order existed; Merryman 1861: circuit court; Nixon 1974: complied). The criterion additionally excludes 'slow-walking with a colorable legal argument', which is the modal real-world behaviour and the only thing observed to date. 8% still prices a 3x uplift over the historical rate.

specific_corrections.claim: 13% by 2031 of an armed state-vs-federal confrontation producing a death or a gunpoint detention
specific_corrections.evidence: Implied 2.6%/yr against zero fatal state-vs-federal armed clashes in ~150 years. Rule of three on 0 events in 150 years gives a 95% upper bound of 3/150 = 2.0%/yr — the model's implied hazard exceeds the upper confidence bound of its own reference class. Little Rock 1957 and Ole Miss 1962-63 are the nearest analogues and both terminated via federalization without an exchange of fire, i.e. the historical resolution mechanism is de-escalation.

specific_corrections.claim: 20% by 2031 of a state-attributed cyberattack cutting power to 1m+ people for 24h+ in NATO/OECD
specific_corrections.evidence: Implied 4.1%/yr against the model's own anchor of 'well under 1%/yr'. The entire world record is Ukraine Dec-2015 (230k customers, ~6h) and Kyiv Dec-2016 (~1h): the population x duration product is 2-3 orders of magnitude short, achieved against the most exposed grid in Europe after years of pre-positioned access. Decisive missing evidence: no intermediate event (100k people, 6h) has ever occurred in a NATO state. A true 4%/yr hazard at the 1M/24h level would imply multiple observed intermediate events; observed count is zero in 11 years of demonstrated capability.

specific_corrections.claim: 20% by 2031 of physical sabotage cutting 500k+ customers for 24h+ in an OECD country
specific_corrections.evidence: Implied 4.1%/yr against the model's own anchor: 5-8 notable attacks in 13 years, largest outage 45,000 customers (Moore County 2022), 'zero at the 500k threshold, base rate under 1%/yr'. That is a 4x uplift over a self-stated rate. Also note this node and geopolitics_grid_cyberattack_nato jointly assign ~36% to a major OECD grid-down event by 2031 by adversarial means, while the catalog contains no node at all for the better-evidenced natural pathway (geomagnetic storm).

specific_corrections.claim: 70% by 2031 of a 30+ day episode with Hormuz crude transit below 50% of baseline
specific_corrections.evidence: Nesting inversion: this is the STRICTEST of three Hormuz nodes (>=30 days sub-50%) yet carries the HIGHEST probability — 70% versus economy_hormuz_closure at 22% (same 50% threshold, only 14 days) and energy_hormuz_reclosure at 34% (14 days). P(30-day) must be <= P(14-day) by construction. Worse, params/duplicate_families.json elects this node as the family representative and suppresses the other two, so the most dramatic and least logically coherent member is what the simulation actually consumes. Historical anchor: never closed at this threshold in 60 years, including 450 ships hit during the 1984-88 Tanker War. 42% reconciles the family upward from the 14-day nodes while respecting the ordering.

specific_corrections.claim: 30% by 2031 of a verified 3-hour sustained wet-bulb 35C observation
specific_corrections.evidence: Implied 6.6%/yr for an event with zero confirmed instances in 45 years, out of roughly 1,000 documented station-hours of brief (1-2h) exceedance. The criterion also requires quality control plus peer-reviewed or national-met-service confirmation, which adds a multi-year publication lag on top of the physical event. The model's own contrarian case notes the binding constraint may be instrumentation — which lowers the RESOLVABLE probability even where it raises the physical one.

specific_corrections.claim: 4% by 2031 of NSIDC daily extent below 1.0 million km2
specific_corrections.evidence: Requires a ~77% single-year collapse from a 4.2-4.7 million km2 September minimum. The largest single-year drop in 47 years of satellite record is 2012 at -18%. The 1979-2026 trend of -0.08 million km2/yr places the central crossing in the 2050s-2060s; even the earliest-tail literature clusters in the 2030s. Under the model's own continuous arctic node (drift -0.06, vol 0.42) this is roughly a 7-sigma excursion by 2031.

specific_corrections.claim: 42% by 2031 that China demonstrates a domestic EUV scanner patterning wafers in a production fab
specific_corrections.evidence: The model's own anchor: ASML took ~17 years from program start to HVM with an unsanctioned global supply chain (Zeiss optics, Cymer sources, TRUMPF lasers), and Soviet/Chinese replication of monopoly capital equipment historically ran 10-20 years behind. China's program is 6-8 years old, so by 2031 it is 11-13 years old under export controls that deny precisely the subsystems ASML did not have to build alone. Base rate of a second national entrant to EUV in 20 years: zero, including Japan and South Korea, who were not sanctioned. The criterion further requires a commercial production fab, not a lab demonstration.

specific_corrections.claim: 15% by 2031 that a G7 country cuts permanent immigration by three quarters
specific_corrections.evidence: The model's own anchor gives 1-2% per country-decade, i.e. 4-8% across 7 countries over the 0.54-decade window before any adjustment — the posted 15% is a 2-3x uplift stated without an evidence budget. Only two clean precedents in a century (Johnson-Reed 1924, the 1930s administrative shutdown). Observed current moves are an order of magnitude smaller: Canada's PR target cut is ~21%, and the deepest modern US single-year fall (FY2020, a pandemic year with consulates closed) was ~40%, not 75%.

specific_corrections.claim: 33% by 2031 that youth-led protests topple 3+ SSA governments in a 36-month window
specific_corrections.evidence: The model's own anchor is 0.19 qualifying removals/yr continent-wide (Burkina 2014, Sudan 2019, Madagascar 2025). Poisson at that rate gives P(>=3 in a 36-month window) = 2.1%. Reaching 33% cumulative over 5.4 years requires sustaining roughly 3x the historical rate for the entire window — a contagion assumption the reasoning asserts but does not evidence beyond one recent cluster. 20% already embeds a 2.5x contagion multiplier.

specific_corrections.claim: 76% by 2031 of a 10%+ epizootic-driven drop in a G20 poultry or pig inventory
specific_corrections.evidence: The model's own anchor says '6-7 events in 12 years across the G20, roughly 50-55%/yr'. At 52%/yr, P(at least one in 5.42 years) = 1 - exp(-0.52*5.42) = 94%. The posted 76% implies 26%/yr — the model halved its own stated frequency with no justification. Qualifying events have occurred in 2015, 2019, 2021, 2022 and 2024-25; the HPAI panzootic is currently active in wild birds on every continent.

specific_corrections.claim: 12% by 2031 that a newly emerged pathogen causes 1m+ cumulative deaths
specific_corrections.evidence: Implied 2.36%/yr against the model's own post-1970 anchor of 3.6%/yr (HIV, COVID in 56 years), which gives 17.9% over 5.42 years. The stated haircut is 'improved countermeasures' — an adjustment COVID directly falsified, having killed ~7m with modern countermeasures inside the post-1970 window that generated the anchor. This is the highest-severity node in the health domain (sev 10) and it is priced below its own reference class.

specific_corrections.claim: 19% by 2031 that WHO declares an influenza pandemic
specific_corrections.evidence: The 19% reproduces a Poisson lambda of 0.04/yr derived from 4-5 recognized pandemics in 108 years. But the criterion is strictly broader than 'recognized pandemic': it also fires on a PHEIC for a novel influenza A with sustained transmission in two WHO regions — a lower bar than the reference class that generated lambda. WHO's post-2009 declaration threshold is also demonstrably lower (8 PHEICs in 17 years across all pathogens). Conditioning on an unprecedented H5N1 panzootic in dairy cattle and poultry, 26% (5.5%/yr) is the coherent number.

specific_corrections.claim: 26% by 2031 of failure or extraordinary rescue of a >$250bn bank
specific_corrections.evidence: Implied 5.5%/yr against the model's own anchor of 'roughly 10% per year unconditionally' (two clusters in 20 years: 2008, 2023), which compounds to 42% over 5.42 years. The stated discount is post-2023 capital and HQLA — but the criterion explicitly counts state-brokered mergers, extraordinary capital injections and bespoke central bank facilities, which is exactly what stronger, faster authorities produce. Better capitalization shifts mass from the 'failure' branch to the 'rescue' branch that the criterion also captures; it does not remove it.

specific_corrections.claim: 12% by 2031 of a successful assassination of a sitting senior US federal official
specific_corrections.evidence: Implied 2.35%/yr against the model's own anchor of ~3%/yr (JFK 1963, Rep. Leo Ryan 1978 in 63 years), which gives 15.7% over the window. The model then discounts below its own base rate while simultaneously listing an escalating attempt series (Giffords 2011, Scalise 2017, Trump 2024 x2) and pricing politics_us_mass_casualty_political_attack at 60%. Attempt frequency is the leading indicator and it is rising, so the correct adjustment from 3%/yr is upward, not downward.

specific_corrections.claim: 15% by 2031 that Xi ceases to be CCP General Secretary for 60+ days
specific_corrections.evidence: The base_rate_anchor is defective: it counts 'irregular removal of a sitting CCP paramount leader — Hua Guofeng is the only clean post-1949 case, ~1.4%/decade'. But the criterion asks about the General Secretary post, and Hu Yaobang (1987) and Zhao Ziyang (1989) were both sitting General Secretaries removed mid-term. Three removals in 76 years is ~3.9%/yr, not 0.14%/yr — a ~28x understatement of the political term. Adding actuarial mortality for a 73-year-old male with elite care (~2%/yr) gives a combined 4-6%/yr, i.e. 20-28% over 5.42 years. Note the current 15% is barely above pure actuarial death risk (~10%), implying ~5% for all political removal over five years.

specific_corrections.claim: 60% by 2031 of a single US ideologically motivated attack killing 10+
specific_corrections.evidence: The model's own anchor lists 8 events in 31 years = ~26%/yr, which gives 76% over 5.42 years; it then adopts the lower recent-five-year rate (~15%/yr) to justify 60%. Selecting the low sub-sample is unjustified in a scenario the same catalog describes as containing rising political violence, an Insurrection Act fight (42%) and an assassination environment. Even a blended 22%/yr gives 70%.

specific_corrections.claim: 11% by 2031 of an INES Level 5+ event at a civil reactor or spent fuel facility
specific_corrections.evidence: Implied 2.15%/yr, which is below the model's own stated post-1990 rate of 2.8%/yr (1 event in 36 years) — before the upward adjustment for war risk that the anchor says it applies. Full-record rate is 4 events in ~70 years = 5.7%/yr. Global reactor count has grown roughly tenfold since the early record, Zaporizhzhia sits in an active war zone with repeated offsite-power losses, and a large newbuild and life-extension wave is underway. 16% corresponds to ~3.2%/yr, i.e. the post-1990 rate plus the war-risk adjustment the model claimed but did not make.

specific_corrections.claim: 30% by 2031 of a new US-Russia deployed-warhead cap
specific_corrections.evidence: Six agreements in 54 years is ~11%/yr unconditional, giving 45% over 5.42 years. The criterion is deliberately permissive — it counts a 'formal reciprocal political commitment announced by both heads of state', requiring no ratification and no verification, which is a far cheaper instrument than the treaties that generated the base rate. The window also contains the model's own near-necessary precondition (Ukraine ceasefire at 78%) and a US presidential election. A full decade with no cap of any kind, including a communique, would be the longest gap since 1972.

specific_corrections.claim: 33% by 2031 that FAO FPI exceeds 160 in any month, versus foodwater_ffpi_above_160 at 42% for the identical threshold on the identical index
specific_corrections.evidence: params/duplicate_families.json itself flags these as a 'duplicate' family with the note 'Identical threshold on the identical index', yet the two nodes carry a 9-point spread and the resolver simply elects the higher one (42%) and suppresses the lower.
